lessons.title: 325. Lesson 13 Presentation 2: skill integration
lessons.subtitle: 张力和章丽 · 玩具熊 · 什么是出关？什么是入关？

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening and Writing)
explanations.body: A. Listen to the dialogs and fill in the table for Travelers 1 to 5: purpose of visit; intended length of stay; location of stay; items to declare (Y/N); first time to China (Y/N); documents mentioned. B. Pair up, take turns sharing the information you entered and discuss the differences. (Audio, not included.)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading, Speaking and Listening): Story 1
explanations.body: A. Pair up. Two Chinese people are talking about their experiences with foreign customs; each partner reads one of the stories (use your dictionary when necessary). B. Without rereading, tell your story to your partner, then mark the statements true or false. The book writes the shared pinyin name as Zhang Li; because every spoken line here is Chinese only, the Chinese line says 都是一样的 (“is the same”) and the spelling is kept in the English line.

examples.text: 我叫张力，我太太叫章丽，汉字不一样，可是写成拼音都是一样的。所以在护照和机票上，我们的名字是一样的。有一次在法国海关，工作人员问我：“你为什么一个人买两张机票？”我说：“有一张是我太太的，我们的名字一样。”海关人员说：“你们的姓当然是一样的，可是名怎么会一样呢？”我说：“我们的姓和名都一样。”她不相信：“男人和女人的名怎么会一样？”我解释说：“我们的名字发音是一样的，但不是同一个字，意思不一样。”她很怀疑地看着我，又拿着我们的机票和护照看了很长时间，还给她的上司打了个电话。最后，她说：“把你们的中文名字写下来。”我把那几个汉字写了下来，她看了半天，最后终于让我们过了海关。她一边在护照上盖章一边说：“你们中国人的名字真有意思！”
examples.translation: wǒ jiào zhāng lì wǒ tài tài jiào zhāng lì hàn zì bù yí yàng kě shì xiě chéng pīn yīn dōu shì yí yàng de suǒ yǐ zài hù zhào hé jī piào shàng wǒ men de míng zì shì yí yàng de yǒu yí cì zài fǎ guó hǎi guān gōng zuò rén yuán wèn wǒ nǐ wèi shén me yí gè rén mǎi liǎng zhāng jī piào wǒ shuō yǒu yì zhāng shì wǒ tài tài de wǒ men de míng zì yí yàng hǎi guān rén yuán shuō nǐ men de xìng dāng rán shì yí yàng de kě shì míng zěn me huì yí yàng ne wǒ shuō wǒ men de xìng hé míng dōu yí yàng tā bù xiāng xìn nán rén hé nǚ rén de míng zěn me huì yí yàng wǒ jiě shì shuō wǒ men de míng zì fā yīn shì yí yàng de dàn bú shì tóng yí gè zì yì si bù yí yàng tā hěn huái yí dì kàn zhe wǒ yòu ná zhe wǒ men de jī piào hé hù zhào kàn le hěn cháng shí jiān hái gěi tā de shàng sī dǎ le gè diàn huà zuì hòu tā shuō bǎ nǐ men de zhōng wén míng zì xiě xià lái wǒ bǎ nà jǐ gè hàn zì xiě le xià lái tā kàn le bàn tiān zuì hòu zhōng yú ràng wǒ men guò le hǎi guān tā yì biān zài hù zhào shàng gài zhāng yì biān shuō nǐ men zhōng guó rén de míng zì zhēn yǒu yì si — My name is Zhang Li and my wife’s name is Zhang Li too (different characters), but written in pinyin both are Zhang Li. So on our passports and plane tickets our names are the same. Once at French customs the officer asked me: “Why are you, one person, buying two tickets?” I said: “One of them is my wife’s; our names are the same.” The customs officer said: “Your surnames are of course the same, but how can your given names be the same?” I said: “Our surnames and given names are both the same.” She didn’t believe it: “How can a man’s and a woman’s given names be the same?” I explained: “Our names sound the same, but they aren’t the same characters and the meanings are different.” She looked at me doubtfully, held our tickets and passports and looked at them for a long time, and even phoned her superior. In the end she said: “Write down your Chinese names.” I wrote the characters down, she looked at them for a long while, and finally let us through customs. As she stamped our passports she said: “Your Chinese people’s names are really interesting!”

explanations.title: Story 2
explanations.body: Story 2 and its statements (my key: 1. True. 2. False, only two officers are mentioned. 3. False, the officer just wanted a picture. 4. False. 5. False, he took a picture of himself with the bear):

examples.text: 有一次我从成都坐飞机到旧金山，下飞机以后，很多中国人排队过海关。站在我前面的女孩抱着一个很可爱的玩具熊。有一个小胖子工作人员走过来问：“这只玩具熊是你的？”女孩儿有点儿紧张，说：“是我的。”那个工作人员说：“你在这儿等着，我很快就回来。”说完他就跑去叫另一位工作人员，然后两个人一起往这边跑来。大家都紧张起来，有什么问题吗？在熊的肚子里有什么东西吗？毒品？很多现金？或者是中国人出国爱带的食品药品什么的？这时，小胖子工作人员把手机给同事，说：“来，给我和这只熊照张相！”
examples.translation: yǒu yí cì wǒ cóng chéng dū zuò fēi jī dào jiù jīn shān xià fēi jī yǐ hòu hěn duō zhōng guó rén pái duì guò hǎi guān zhàn zài wǒ qián miàn de nǚ hái bào zhe yí gè hěn kě ài de wán jù xióng yǒu yí gè xiǎo pàng zi gōng zuò rén yuán zǒu guò lái wèn zhè zhǐ wán jù xióng shì nǐ de nǚ hái ér yǒu diǎnr jǐn zhāng shuō shì wǒ de nà ge gōng zuò rén yuán shuō nǐ zài zhèr děng zhe wǒ hěn kuài jiù huí lái shuō wán tā jiù pǎo qù jiào lìng yí wèi gōng zuò rén yuán rán hòu liǎng gè rén yì qǐ wǎng zhè biān pǎo lái dà jiā dōu jǐn zhāng qǐ lái yǒu shén me wèn tí ma zài xióng de dǔ zi lǐ yǒu shén me dōng xī ma dú pǐn hěn duō xiàn jīn huò zhě shì zhōng guó rén chū guó ài dài de shí pǐn yào pǐn shén me de zhè shí xiǎo pàng zi gōng zuò rén yuán bǎ shǒu jī gěi tóng shì shuō lái gěi wǒ hé zhè zhǐ xióng zhào zhāng xiāng — Once I flew from Chengdu to San Francisco, and after getting off the plane many Chinese people queued up for customs. The girl standing in front of me was holding a very cute teddy bear (wánjùxióng). A chubby staff member came over and asked: “Is this teddy bear yours?” The girl was a bit nervous and said: “It’s mine.” The staff member said: “Wait here, I’ll be back soon.” After saying that he ran off to call another staff member, and then the two of them ran over this way together. Everyone got nervous: was there a problem? Was there something inside the bear’s belly? Drugs? A lot of cash? Or the food and medicine Chinese people like to take abroad? Just then the chubby staff member handed his phone to his colleague and said: “Come on, take a picture of me and this bear!”

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading, Speaking and Writing)
explanations.body: A. Below is an answer posted online about international travel (什么是出关？什么是入关？). Read it and note any unknown words. B. Highlight the words you think are critical for understanding the passage and guess their meaning; compare with a classmate. C. Do you think the text defines the terms clearly? If not, type in your own definition of 出关 and 入关. My definitions: 出关 is completing the exit formalities (passport and visa check) when leaving a country; 入关 is completing the entry formalities on arrival (forms, officer’s questions, luggage inspection, passport stamp).

examples.text: 比如你从杭州的萧山机场去南非看世界杯，要是你已经有签证，你就要办理出关手续。等你飞了十多个小时，到了南非约翰内斯堡机场。你就要办理入关手续。在快到目的地的时候，空乘会让旅客填写一些表。下飞机以后，就要办理入关手续，海关官员会问你一些问题，比如你为什么要来南非，住在什么地方，什么时候离开。还会检查行李，要是都没有问题，他们会在你护照上盖章。你就正式到达了南非，可以去看比赛了。
examples.translation: bǐ rú nǐ cóng háng zhōu de xiāo shān jī chǎng qù nán fēi kàn shì jiè bēi yào shì nǐ yǐ jīng yǒu qiān zhèng nǐ jiù yào bàn lǐ chū guān shǒu xù děng nǐ fēi le shí duō gè xiǎo shí dào le nán fēi yuē hàn nèi sī bǎo jī chǎng nǐ jiù yào bàn lǐ rù guān shǒu xù zài kuài dào mù dì dì de shí hòu kōng chéng huì ràng lǚ kè tián xiě yì xiē biǎo xià fēi jī yǐ hòu jiù yào bàn lǐ rù guān shǒu xù hǎi guān guān yuán huì wèn nǐ yì xiē wèn tí bǐ rú nǐ wèi shén me yào lái nán fēi zhù zài shén me dì fāng shén me shí hòu lí kāi hái huì jiǎn chá xíng li yào shì dōu méi yǒu wèn tí tā men huì zài nǐ hù zhào shàng gài zhāng nǐ jiù zhèng shì dào dá le nán fēi kě yǐ qù kàn bǐ sài le — For example, if you go from Hangzhou’s Xiaoshan Airport to South Africa to watch the World Cup and you already have a visa, you have to go through exit procedures. After you have flown for more than ten hours and arrived at Johannesburg airport in South Africa, you have to go through entry procedures. When you are about to arrive at the destination, the flight attendants have passengers fill out some forms. After getting off the plane you go through entry procedures; customs officials ask you some questions, such as why you are coming to South Africa, where you will stay and when you will leave. They also inspect your luggage, and if everything is fine they stamp your passport. You have officially arrived in South Africa and can go watch the matches.

explanations.title: The 外国人入境卡

explanations.title: Activities 2 and 3
explanations.body: Activity 2 (Reading and Writing). A. Work in groups of three. One group plays customs officers for three places: 中国, 新加坡 and 台湾; the other group plays the travelers, each going to be interviewed by all three officers using their character’s information from Activity 1. The officers use the Customs Recording Sheet (Name, Nationality, Purpose of Visit, Intended Length of Stay, Location of Stay, Items to Declare? (Y/N), First Time? (Y/N)) to record each traveler’s information and sign the traveler’s visa after granting entry. B. The two groups switch roles and repeat. Activity 3 (Reading and Speaking). Pair up. Another form you must fill out before arriving is a customs declaration form. Read the sample form (a picture, not included) without using your dictionary and discuss with your partner what items must be declared if you are traveling to China.

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss: A. What articles are not allowed on an airplane? B. Have you ever had anything confiscated at the airport security gate? C. Have you ever experienced complications at the security checkpoint? What was the problem? D. Have you ever missed a flight? Why?

explanations.title: Presentation 3: a missed flight
explanations.body: (The book also prints this passage in traditional characters. The book writes the time as 40 分钟; it is spelled out here.)

examples.text: “九一一”以前，乘坐航班很方便，拿到登机牌后，可以直接上飞机。现在登机前要过安检，一些人因此误了航班。去年夏天，我坐飞机去纽约看朋友。我已经在网上办好了登机手续，所以只提前了四十分钟到机场。到了机场才发现过安检要排很长的队。因为离飞机起飞只有半个小时了，我只好请排在前边的人让我往前站。大家看到我着急的样子，都让开路，让我站到了最前边。可是，过安检的时候，安检人员要检查我的背包。原来，里面有一瓶没喝完的水。过了安检，我飞快地跑到登机口，可是机门已经关了。唉，要是我早一点儿出门，就不会误机了！
examples.translation: jiǔ yī yī yǐ qián chéng zuò háng bān hěn fāng biàn ná dào dēng jī pái hòu kě yǐ zhí jiē shàng fēi jī xiàn zài dēng jī qián yào guò ān jiǎn yì xiē rén yīn cǐ wù le háng bān qù nián xià tiān wǒ zuò fēi jī qù niǔ yuē kàn péng yǒu wǒ yǐ jīng zài wǎng shàng bàn hǎo le dēng jī shǒu xù suǒ yǐ zhǐ tí qián le sì shí fēn zhōng dào jī chǎng dào le jī chǎng cái fā xiàn guò ān jiǎn yào pái hěn cháng de duì yīn wèi lí fēi jī qǐ fēi zhǐ yǒu bàn gè xiǎo shí le wǒ zhǐ hǎo qǐng pái zài qián biān de rén ràng wǒ wǎng qián zhàn dà jiā kàn dào wǒ zháo jí de yàng zi dōu ràng kāi lù ràng wǒ zhàn dào le zuì qián biān kě shì guò ān jiǎn de shí hòu ān jiǎn rén yuán yào jiǎn chá wǒ de bēi bāo yuán lái lǐ miàn yǒu yì píng méi hē wán de shuǐ guò le ān jiǎn wǒ fēi kuài dì pǎo dào dēng jī kǒu kě shì jī mén yǐ jīng guān le āi yào shì wǒ zǎo yì diǎnr chū mén jiù bú huì wù jī le — Before 9/11, taking a flight was very convenient: after getting your boarding pass, you could board the plane directly. Now you have to go through security before boarding, and as a result some people miss their flights. Last summer I flew to New York to see a friend. I had already checked in online, so I arrived at the airport only forty minutes early. After arriving I found that going through security meant standing in a very long line. Because only half an hour was left before takeoff, I had no choice but to ask the people ahead of me to let me move forward. When everyone saw my anxious look, they all made way and let me stand at the very front. But when I went through security, the security staff wanted to check my backpack. As it turned out, there was a bottle of water I hadn’t finished inside. After security I ran to the boarding gate as fast as I could, but the airplane door had already closed. Ah, if only I had left home a little earlier, I wouldn’t have missed the flight!

explanations.title: Activities 1 and 2
explanations.body: Activity 1 (Listening). A. Global listening: 1. What are the repercussions of 9/11 at airports now? 2. What did the speaker say happened at the end of the passage? B. Detailed listening: what caused the speaker to miss the flight? List three details. (Audio, not included. From the text: people now must pass security, so some miss flights; the speaker ended up missing the flight because he arrived late for a long security line, a bottle of water was found in his bag, and the plane door had closed when he got to the gate.) Activity 2 (Reading). A. Using what you heard, list the nine events in order of occurrence. B. Pair up, read your sorted sentences and discuss any differences. The book’s nine items are listed in the table in the book’s order; my sorted order (mine) is the second table.

(Audio, not included.) Activity 4 (Reading, Writing and Speaking). A. Pair up and write short scenarios with dialog using the information provided. Scene 1 is given as an example (location: airport check-in desk; characters: David and the check-in agent; time: 9:30 a.m.). Scene 2 is at the airport security checkpoint, 9:40 a.m. (David and other passengers lining up); Scene 3 is at the check-in desk per the book, 9:45 a.m. (David and a security officer); Scene 4 is at the boarding gate, 10:00 a.m. (David and the boarding gate agent). B. Act out the skits in order. The book’s Scene 1 and my brief Scenes 2 to 4:

examples.translation: dà wèi wǒ yǐ jīng zài wǎng shàng bàn lǐ dēng jī shǒu xù le zhè shì wǒ de dēng jī pái — David: I already checked in online. Here is my boarding pass.

examples.text: 工作人员：请把行李箱放到这里称一下。
examples.translation: gōng zuò rén yuán qǐng bǎ xíng li xiāng fàng dào zhè lǐ chēng yí xià — Staff: Please put the suitcase here to be weighed.

examples.text: 大卫：没超重吧？
examples.translation: dà wèi méi chāo zhòng ba — David: It isn’t overweight, is it?

examples.text: 工作人员：没有。这是您的行李牌。不过，你得快点儿去安检和登机。
examples.translation: gōng zuò rén yuán méi yǒu zhè shì nín de xíng li pái bú guò nǐ děi kuài diǎnr qù ān jiǎn hé dēng jī — Staff: No. Here is your luggage tag. But you have to hurry to security and boarding.

examples.text: 大卫跑到安检处，前面排着很长的队。他很着急，请前面的人让他先过。
examples.translation: dà wèi pǎo dào ān jiǎn chù qián miàn pái zhe hěn cháng de duì tā hěn zháo jí qǐng qián miàn de rén ràng tā xiān guò — David runs to the security checkpoint, where a long line has formed. He is anxious and asks the people ahead to let him go first. (my Scene 2 description)

examples.text: 安检人员：请把背包放在这里。里面有水吗？
examples.translation: ān jiǎn rén yuán qǐng bǎ bēi bāo fàng zài zhè lǐ lǐ miàn yǒu shuǐ ma — Security officer: Please put your backpack here. Is there water inside? (my Scene 3)

examples.text: 大卫：有一瓶没喝完的水。对不起，我忘了。
examples.translation: dà wèi yǒu yì píng méi hē wán de shuǐ duì bù qǐ wǒ wàng le — David: There is a bottle of water I haven’t finished. Sorry, I forgot. (my Scene 3)

examples.text: 登机口工作人员：对不起，机门已经关了。
examples.translation: dēng jī kǒu gōng zuò rén yuán duì bù qǐ jī mén yǐ jīng guān le — Gate agent: Sorry, the plane door has already closed. (my Scene 4)

examples.text: 大卫：唉，要是我早一点儿出门就好了！
examples.translation: dà wèi āi yào shì wǒ zǎo yì diǎnr chū mén jiù hǎo le — David: Ah, if only I had left earlier! (my Scene 4)

lessons.title: 329. Lesson 13 Presentation 3 grammar: 的样子
lessons.subtitle: 我要记住你的样子 · 你笑的样子真好看 · 好像要下雨的样子

explanations.title: 的样子
explanations.body: 的样子 can be placed after nouns, pronouns, verbs or adjectives to describe: physical shape, image or appearance; apparent mental state; a standard representation of something for people to see and imitate; and (in spoken language) a condition or trend. Pattern: Noun/Pronoun/Verb/Adjective + 的样子. The book’s notes are in the English lines.

examples.text: 他看起来四十多岁的样子。
examples.translation: tā kàn qǐ lái sì shí duō suì de yàng zi — He looks about forty. (noun + 样子, physical appearance)

examples.text: 我要记住你的样子。
examples.translation: wǒ yào jì zhù nǐ de yàng zi — I want to remember how you look. (pronoun + 样子, physical appearance)

examples.text: 照我的样子打球。
examples.translation: zhào wǒ de yàng zi dǎ qiú — Play ball the way I do. (pronoun + 样子, standard for imitation)

examples.text: 我喜欢她笑的样子。
examples.translation: wǒ xǐ huān tā xiào de yàng zi — I like the way she smiles. (verb + 样子, physical appearance)

examples.text: 他看起来很着急的样子。
examples.translation: tā kàn qǐ lái hěn zháo jí de yàng zi — He looks very anxious. (adjective + 样子, apparent mental state)

examples.text: 好像要下雨的样子。
examples.translation: hǎo xiàng yào xià yǔ de yàng zi — It looks like it’s going to rain. (verb + 样子, condition or trend)

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading)
explanations.body: Translate the sentences into English (the book glosses 好像 hǎoxiàng seem, 生气 shēng qì angry, 吓人 xiàrén scary, 显出 xiǎnchū appear, 海员 sailor, 难看 nánkàn ugly). The twelve sentences are listed here with my translations (mine):

examples.text: 看你的样子好像没睡好觉。
examples.translation: kàn nǐ de yàng zi hǎo xiàng méi shuì hǎo jiào — You look like you didn’t sleep well.

examples.text: 我喜欢那个房子的样子。
examples.translation: wǒ xǐ huān nà ge fáng zi de yàng zi — I like the look of that house.

examples.text: 他生气的样子很吓人。
examples.translation: tā shēng qì de yàng zi hěn xià rén — He looks scary when he’s angry.

examples.text: 你笑的样子真好看。
examples.translation: nǐ xiào de yàng zi zhēn hǎo kàn — You look really good when you smile.

examples.text: 看他的样子，一定是跟女朋友分手了。
examples.translation: kàn tā de yàng zi yí dìng shì gēn nǚ péng yǒu fēn shǒu le — Judging by how he looks, he must have broken up with his girlfriend.

examples.text: 他没有要停下来的样子。
examples.translation: tā méi yǒu yào tíng xià lái de yàng zi — He shows no sign of stopping.

examples.text: 他的样子有了很大的变化。
examples.translation: tā de yàng zi yǒu le hěn dà de biàn huà — His appearance has changed a lot.

examples.text: 他好像很有钱的样子。
examples.translation: tā hǎo xiàng hěn yǒu qián de yàng zi — He seems to be rich.

examples.text: 他显出不高兴的样子。
examples.translation: tā xiǎn chū bù gāo xìng de yàng zi — He showed an unhappy look.

examples.text: 他走路的样子像个海员。
examples.translation: tā zǒu lù de yàng zi xiàng gè hǎi yuán — The way he walks is like a sailor’s.

examples.text: 他吃东西的样子很难看。
examples.translation: tā chī dōng xī de yàng zi hěn nán kàn — The way he eats is ugly.

examples.text: 你好像很累的样子。
examples.translation: nǐ hǎo xiàng hěn lèi de yàng zi — You look very tired.

options: Appearance, apparent mental state, a model to imitate, or a trend

exercises.prompt: What does 我要记住你的样子 mean?
options: I want to be like you
I want to see you tomorrow
I want to remember how you look

exercises.prompt: What does 照我的样子打球 mean?
options: Play ball the way I do

exercises.prompt: What does 好像要下雨的样子 mean?
options: It looks like it’s going to rain

exercises.prompt: What does 他看起来很着急的样子 mean?
options: He is not in a hurry

exercises.prompt: What does 他没有要停下来的样子 mean?
options: He shows no sign of stopping

options: The way he walks is like a sailor’s

lessons.title: 330. Lesson 13 Presentation 3 grammar: the resultative complement 到
lessons.subtitle: 回到家 · 看到十二点半 · 放到桌子上去 · 买到车票

explanations.title: Resultative Complement 到
explanations.body: The resultative complement 到 indicates that the action of the verb preceding the complement reaches a given point, in either space or time. In its extended meaning, it also indicates successfully acquiring something. Affirmative: Subj. + Verb + 到 + Obj. Negative: Subj. + 没（有）+ Verb + 到 + Obj.

examples.text: 我回到家就上床睡觉了。
examples.translation: wǒ huí dào jiā jiù shàng chuáng shuì jiào le — As soon as I got home I went to bed.

examples.text: 我昨天晚上看电视看到十二点半。
examples.translation: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shàng kàn diàn shì kàn dào shí èr diǎn bàn — Last night I watched TV until 12:30.

examples.text: 把碗和筷子放到桌子上去。
examples.translation: bǎ wǎn hé kuài zi fàng dào zhuō zi shàng qù — Put the bowls and chopsticks on the table.

examples.text: 甲：你买到车票了吗？
examples.translation: jiǎ nǐ mǎi dào chē piào le ma — Did you manage to buy a ticket?

examples.text: 乙：我没有买到星期五的票，买到星期六的了。
examples.translation: yǐ wǒ méi yǒu mǎi dào xīng qī wǔ de piào mǎi dào xīng qī liù de le — I couldn’t get a Friday ticket; I got a Saturday one.

explanations.title: Activities 2 and 3
explanations.body: Activity 2 (Listening). Listen to four short dialogs: 1. What was the male speaker’s request? 2. When will the phone call be made and to which number? 3. Is there an airplane present? How can you tell? 4. What is the male speaker’s problem and its cause? (Audio, not included.) Activity 3 (Reading). Read the short dialogs and complete the sentences using verbs with the correct resultative complements 完, 好 and 到, including negative forms. The book leaves the blanks; my completed dialogs:

examples.text: 甲：你们照相照完了没有？饭菜都做好了，要吃饭了。
examples.translation: jiǎ nǐ men zhào xiàng zhào wán le méi yǒu fàn cài dōu zuò hǎo le yào chī fàn le — Have you finished taking pictures? The meal is all prepared; it’s time to eat.

examples.text: 乙：照完了。我把照相机收好就来。
examples.translation: yǐ zhào wán le wǒ bǎ zhào xiàng jī shōu hǎo jiù lái — Done. I’ll come as soon as I put the camera away.

examples.text: 甲：那袋糖放哪儿了？你妹妹找不到。
examples.translation: jiǎ nà dài táng fàng nǎr le nǐ mèi mèi zhǎo bú dào — Where did the bag of sweets go? Your sister can’t find it.

examples.text: 乙：我已经吃完了。
examples.translation: yǐ wǒ yǐ jīng chī wán le — I’ve already finished it.

examples.text: 甲：你都吃完了？
examples.translation: jiǎ nǐ dōu chī wán le — You finished it all?

examples.text: 乙：对不起。我想再去买一袋的，可是没买到。那种糖已经卖完了。
examples.translation: yǐ duì bù qǐ wǒ xiǎng zài qù mǎi yí dài de kě shì méi mǎi dào nà zhǒng táng yǐ jīng mài wán le — Sorry. I wanted to go buy another bag, but I couldn’t get any. That kind of candy is sold out.

examples.text: 甲：小文，那本书你买到了吗？
examples.translation: jiǎ xiǎo wén nà běn shū nǐ mǎi dào le ma — Xiaowen, did you get that book?

examples.text: 乙：没买到。我去书店的时候，已经卖完了。
examples.translation: yǐ méi mǎi dào wǒ qù shū diàn de shí hòu yǐ jīng mài wán le — No. By the time I went to the bookstore, it was sold out.

examples.text: 甲：我跟大年说好了，今天下课以后去东风书店看看。你跟我们一起去吧。
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ gēn dà nián shuō hǎo le jīn tiān xià kè yǐ hòu qù dōng fēng shū diàn kàn kàn nǐ gēn wǒ men yì qǐ qù ba — I’ve arranged with Danian to go to Dongfeng Bookstore after class today. Come with us.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Writing and Reading)
explanations.body: 小文 is texting his friend to see when they will arrive for a potluck meal. Translate the responses into Chinese using the appropriate resultative complement, then add more of your own: 1. I will be there as soon as I finish my homework. 2. I will be there after the formation. 3. I cannot find the beer we both like. It’s sold out! 4. We will be there as soon as my girlfriend finds her shoes. 5. Sorry, I am running a little late. I will be there as soon as I get my computer fixed. 6. My wife is cooking. We will be there once she gets this dish cooked. 7. What other reasons might they have? My translations:

examples.text: 我做完作业就到。
examples.translation: wǒ zuò wán zuò yè jiù dào — I’ll be there as soon as I finish my homework.

examples.text: 集合完以后我就到。
examples.translation: jí hé wán yǐ hòu wǒ jiù dào — I’ll be there after the formation.

examples.text: 我找不到我们都喜欢的啤酒。卖完了！
examples.translation: wǒ zhǎo bú dào wǒ men dōu xǐ huān de pí jiǔ mài wán le — I can’t find the beer we both like. It’s sold out!

examples.text: 我女朋友找到鞋子，我们就到。
examples.translation: wǒ nǚ péng yǒu zhǎo dào xié zi wǒ men jiù dào — We’ll be there as soon as my girlfriend finds her shoes.

examples.text: 对不起，我可能会晚一点儿。我修好电脑就到。
examples.translation: duì bù qǐ wǒ kě néng huì wǎn yì diǎnr wǒ xiū hǎo diàn nǎo jiù dào — Sorry, I’ll be a little late. I’ll be there as soon as I get my computer fixed.

examples.text: 我太太在做饭。她做好这个菜，我们就到。
examples.translation: wǒ tài tài zài zuò fàn tā zuò hǎo zhè ge cài wǒ men jiù dào — My wife is cooking. We’ll be there once she gets this dish cooked.

examples.text: 我还没有找到我的手机。
examples.translation: wǒ hái méi yǒu zhǎo dào wǒ de shǒu jī — I haven’t found my phone yet. (my own extra reason)

exercises.prompt: What does the complement 到 indicate?
options: The action reaches a point in space or time, or something is successfully obtained

exercises.prompt: How do you negate a verb with 到?
What does 我回到家就上床睡觉了 mean?
options: As soon as I got home I went to bed
I will go to bed later

exercises.prompt: What does 我昨天晚上看电视看到十二点半 mean?
options: I watched TV until 12:30 last night

exercises.prompt: What does 你买到车票了吗？ ask?
options: Did you manage to get the ticket?

exercises.prompt: What does 我没有买到星期五的票 mean?
options: I didn’t manage to get a Friday ticket

exercises.prompt: Which fits: 我去书店的时候，书已经___了。(sold out)
把碗和筷子放___桌子上去。

lessons.title: 331. Lesson 13 Presentation 3 grammar: 原来
lessons.subtitle: 原来的 · 我原来住在东部 · 原来是你！ · 原来，背包里有一瓶水

explanations.title: 原来
explanations.body: 原来 means “original” or “former” as an adjective, and “originally” as an adverb. As an adverb it can also mean “all along” or “as it turns out” and indicates a sudden realization of something previously unknown. As an adjective: 原来 + 的 + Noun. As an adverb: Subj. + 原来 + Predicate. As “all along”: 原来 + New/True Information. The book’s examples with numbers are spelled out here (999 is 九百九十九).

examples.text: 你原来的短发也很可爱。
examples.translation: nǐ yuán lái de duǎn fà yě hěn kě ài — Your original short hair was cute too.

examples.text: 这件衣服原来的价格是九百九十九块。
examples.translation: zhè jiàn yī fú yuán lái de jià gé shì jiǔ bǎi jiǔ shí jiǔ kuài — This piece of clothing’s original price was 999 yuan.

examples.text: 她现在的男朋友比原来的那位有钱。
examples.translation: tā xiàn zài de nán péng yǒu bǐ yuán lái de nà wèi yǒu qián — Her boyfriend now is richer than the former one.

examples.text: 我没有变，我还是原来的我。
examples.translation: wǒ méi yǒu biàn wǒ hái shì yuán lái de wǒ — I haven’t changed; I’m still the same me.

examples.text: 她原来的工资比现在高。
examples.translation: tā yuán lái de gōng zī bǐ xiàn zài gāo — Her original salary was higher than now.

examples.text: 这是我原来住的地方。
examples.translation: zhè shì wǒ yuán lái zhù de dì fāng — This is where I used to live.

examples.text: 我原来住在东部，几个月前才搬到这里。
examples.translation: wǒ yuán lái zhù zài dōng bù jǐ gè yuè qián cái bān dào zhè lǐ — I used to live in the east and only moved here a few months ago.

examples.text: 他们原来是同学，现在是男女朋友。
examples.translation: tā men yuán lái shì tóng xué xiàn zài shì nán nǚ péng yǒu — They were originally classmates; now they are boyfriend and girlfriend.

examples.text: 我父亲原来也是军人。
examples.translation: wǒ fù qīn yuán lái yě shì jūn rén — My father was also a soldier originally.

examples.text: 我原来不喜欢日本菜，后来觉得日本菜很好。
examples.translation: wǒ yuán lái bù xǐ huān rì běn cài hòu lái jué de rì běn cài hěn hǎo — I originally didn’t like Japanese food; later I found it very good.

examples.text: 原来是你！
examples.translation: yuán lái shì nǐ — So it was you all along!

examples.text: 原来你们认识？
examples.translation: yuán lái nǐ men rèn shí — So you both knew each other this whole time?

examples.text: 原来是这样！
examples.translation: yuán lái shì zhè yàng — Oh, so it’s like that!

examples.text: 原来你这么有钱！
examples.translation: yuán lái nǐ zhè me yǒu qián — It turns out you are so rich!

examples.text: 原来，背包里有一瓶水。
examples.translation: yuán lái bēi bāo lǐ yǒu yì píng shuǐ — It turned out that there was a bottle of water in the backpack.

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Translate the following sentences into English, then pair up and compare answers (the book glosses 难怪 nánguài as “no wonder” and 我说 as “I wondered”). The book’s nine sentences, with my translations:

examples.text: 原来是你啊！我刚才没看出来。
examples.translation: yuán lái shì nǐ a wǒ gāng cái méi kàn chū lái — So it’s you! I didn’t recognize you just now.

examples.text: 他还住在原来的地方。
examples.translation: tā hái zhù zài yuán lái de dì fāng — He still lives in the same place.

examples.text: 我们学会了很多原来不懂的东西。
examples.translation: wǒ men xué huì le hěn duō yuán lái bù dǒng de dōng xī — We’ve learned many things we didn’t understand before.

examples.text: 原来是这样啊，那是我错了。
examples.translation: yuán lái shì zhè yàng a nà shì wǒ cuò le — Oh, so that’s how it is; then I was wrong.

examples.text: 难怪他的中文说得这么好，原来他太太是台湾人。
examples.translation: nán guài tā de zhōng wén shuō de zhè me hǎo yuán lái tā tài tài shì tái wān rén — No wonder his Chinese is so good; it turns out his wife is from Taiwan.

examples.text: 我还是原来的我。
examples.translation: wǒ hái shì yuán lái de wǒ — I’m still the same me.

examples.text: 我说夜里怎么这么冷，原来是下雪了。
examples.translation: wǒ shuō yè lǐ zěn me zhè me lěng yuán lái shì xià xuě le — I wondered why it was so cold at night; it turns out it was snowing.

examples.text: 我原来不习惯这里的生活，现在好多了。
examples.translation: wǒ yuán lái bù xí guàn zhè lǐ de shēng huó xiàn zài hǎo duō le — I originally wasn’t used to life here; now it’s much better.

examples.text: 几十年过去了，我的老家还是原来的样子。
examples.translation: jǐ shí nián guò qù le wǒ de lǎo jiā hái shì yuán lái de yàng zi — Decades have passed and my hometown still looks the way it used to.

exercises.prompt: What does 原来 mean as an adjective?
What does 原来 mean as a sudden realization?
What does 她原来的工资比现在高 mean?
options: Her original salary was higher than now

exercises.prompt: What does 我原来住在东部 mean?
options: I live in the east now
I used to live in the east
I never lived in the east
I will live in the east

exercises.prompt: What does 原来你这么有钱！ express?
options: Surprise: so you are this rich

exercises.prompt: What does 他还住在原来的地方 mean?
options: He still lives in the same place

exercises.prompt: What does 几十年过去了，我的老家还是原来的样子 mean?
options: My hometown has changed a lot
After decades my hometown still looks the way it used to

exercises.prompt: 我没有变，我还是原来的___。
exercises.explanation: 原来的我: the same me.
原来是这样: so that’s how it is.

lessons.title: 332. Lesson 13 Presentation 3 grammar: 因此 versus 所以
lessons.subtitle: 现在登机前要安检，一些人因此误了航班 · 因此 · 所以

explanations.title: 因此
explanations.body: 因此 (literally “because of this”) means “therefore”. Its meaning is similar to 所以, but the usage is different: 因此 is more formal; 因此 can be placed directly after a subject, while 所以 can only be used at the beginning of the result clause; 所以 is compatible with 因为, whereas 因此 is not, because 因此 already includes the meaning of 因为. Patterns: Cause, 因此 + Effect; Cause, Subj. + 因此 + Effect.

examples.text: 现在登机前要安检，一些人因此误了航班。
examples.translation: xiàn zài dēng jī qián yào ān jiǎn yì xiē rén yīn cǐ wù le háng bān — Now there is security before boarding, and some people therefore miss their flights.

examples.text: 小文上课玩儿手机，老师因此批评了他。
examples.translation: xiǎo wén shàng kè wánr shǒu jī lǎo shī yīn cǐ pī píng le tā — Xiaowen played with his phone in class, and the teacher therefore criticized him. (批评 pīpíng: criticize)

examples.text: 蒙特雷很少下雨，因此气候很干旱。
examples.translation: méng tè léi hěn shǎo xià yǔ yīn cǐ qì hòu hěn gān hàn — It seldom rains in Monterey, so the climate is very dry.

examples.text: 这里风景美，天气也好，因此，有很多人到这里旅游。
examples.translation: zhè lǐ fēng jǐng měi tiān qì yě hǎo yīn cǐ yǒu hěn duō rén dào zhè lǐ lǚ yóu — The scenery here is beautiful and the weather is good, so many people come here to travel.

examples.text: 他是家里最小的儿子，因此，他得到了父母最多的爱。
examples.translation: tā shì jiā lǐ zuì xiǎo de ér zi yīn cǐ tā dé dào le fù mǔ zuì duō de ài — He is the youngest son in the family, so he received the most love from his parents.

explanations.title: Activity 6 (Reading)
explanations.body: Match the causes and results and complete the sentences with 因此 and 所以 as needed (both may be used in some sentences), then translate them orally. The causes: 1. 在这个小地方很难找到工作。 2. 小文没有交作业。 3. 李老师讲课讲得很好。 4. 她在重庆出生长大。 5. 他的话让大家都笑了。 6. 因为我有梦想。 7. 他一直不习惯大城市的生活。 The results: A. …，在离开二十年以后，他又回到了老家。 B. 老师…批评了他。 C. 很多年轻人…离开这里去了大城市。 D. …，同学们都喜欢上他的课。 E. …我一直在努力。 F. …她很了解这里的生活。 G. 教室里的气氛…轻松了很多。 The book prints 20 年 as digits. My matches and completions (mine):

examples.text: 在这个小地方很难找到工作，因此很多年轻人离开这里去了大城市。
examples.translation: zài zhè ge xiǎo dì fāng hěn nán zhǎo dào gōng zuò yīn cǐ hěn duō nián qīng rén lí kāi zhè lǐ qù le dà chéng shì — It’s hard to find work in this small place, so many young people have left for big cities. (1→C)

examples.text: 小文没有交作业，老师因此批评了他。
examples.translation: xiǎo wén méi yǒu jiāo zuò yè lǎo shī yīn cǐ pī píng le tā — Xiaowen didn’t hand in his homework, so the teacher criticized him. (2→B)

examples.text: 李老师讲课讲得很好，因此同学们都喜欢上他的课。
examples.translation: lǐ lǎo shī jiǎng kè jiǎng de hěn hǎo yīn cǐ tóng xué men dōu xǐ huān shàng tā de kè — Teacher Li teaches very well, so the students all like his class. (3→D)

examples.text: 她在重庆出生长大，因此她很了解这里的生活。
examples.translation: tā zài chóng qìng chū shēng zhǎng dà yīn cǐ tā hěn liǎo jiě zhè lǐ de shēng huó — She was born and raised in Chongqing, so she understands life here well. (4→F)

examples.text: 他的话让大家都笑了，教室里的气氛因此轻松了很多。
examples.translation: tā de huà ràng dà jiā dōu xiào le jiào shì lǐ de qì fēn yīn cǐ qīng sōng le hěn duō — His words made everyone laugh, and the mood in the classroom became much more relaxed. (5→G)

examples.text: 因为我有梦想，所以我一直在努力。
examples.translation: yīn wèi wǒ yǒu mèng xiǎng suǒ yǐ wǒ yì zhí zài nǔ lì — Because I have a dream, I have been working hard. (6→E: 所以 goes with 因为)

examples.text: 他一直不习惯大城市的生活，所以在离开二十年以后，他又回到了老家。
examples.translation: tā yì zhí bù xí guàn dà chéng shì de shēng huó suǒ yǐ zài lí kāi èr shí nián yǐ hòu tā yòu huí dào le lǎo jiā — He never got used to life in big cities, so after twenty years away he went back to his hometown. (7→A)

explanations.title: Activity 7 (Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Think about answers to the questions below. B. Pair up and share your responses; your partner then reports them to the class using 因此 sentences.

examples.text: 你为什么参军？
examples.translation: nǐ wèi shén me cān jūn — Why did you join the military?

examples.text: 你为什么选择这个军种？
examples.translation: nǐ wèi shén me xuǎn zé zhè ge jūn zhǒng — Why did you choose this service branch?

examples.text: 你喜欢现在的生活吗？为什么？
examples.translation: nǐ xǐ huān xiàn zài de shēng huó ma wèi shén me — Do you like your life now? Why?

exercises.prompt: Where can 因此 go that 所以 cannot?
options: Directly after the subject of the result clause
At the end of a sentence
因为我有梦想，因此，所以努力。
因为我有梦想，因此我一直在努力。
我有梦想，因为所以努力。
因为我有梦想，所以我一直在努力。

exercises.prompt: What does 蒙特雷很少下雨，因此气候很干旱 mean?
options: It seldom rains in Monterey, so the climate is very dry
It rains a lot, so it is humid
Monterey is a dry city but rainy

exercises.prompt: What does 他是家里最小的儿子，因此，他得到了父母最多的爱 mean?
options: He is the oldest son and loved
He’s the youngest son, so he got the most love from his parents
同学们都喜欢上他的课

exercises.prompt: 小文上课玩儿手机，老师因___批评了他。
因为我有梦想，___以我一直在努力。

lessons.title: 333. Lesson 13 Presentation 3 grammar: 要是…就… (if…then…)
lessons.subtitle: 要是…就… · 要是…的话 · 要是…就好了！ · 挤牛奶的女孩

explanations.title: 要是…就… construction (if…then…)
explanations.body: The 要是…就… construction is a very common way to form conditional statements in Chinese. It is very similar to 如果…就… in usage and formality. Pattern: 要是 + Supposed Condition (+ 的话), Subj. + 就 + Response to the Condition. 1. The two clauses can share the same subject or have different subjects. The subject in the conditional clause can be placed either before or after 要是, but the subject in the result clause can only be placed before 就. We do not say * 要是天气不好，就我们不去海边; this is different from the subject’s location in English “if…then…”. 2. Variations: 要是 can be omitted (Sentence 1 below); 要是 can be simplified to 要 to be more colloquial (Sentence 4); “的话” may be added to the end of the conditional clause (Sentence 2); 要是…就好了！ is a fixed expression for “If only…!” (Sentence 5).

examples.text: 我要是早十分钟出门，就不会误机了！
examples.translation: wǒ yào shì zǎo shí fēn zhōng chū mén jiù bú huì wù jī le — If I had left ten minutes earlier, I wouldn’t have missed the flight!

examples.text: 要是有钱的话，我就去很多国家旅行。
examples.translation: yào shì yǒu qián de huà wǒ jiù qù hěn duō guó jiā lǚ xíng — If I had money, I would travel to many countries.

examples.text: 要是我去晚了，你们就先吃，不要等我。
examples.translation: yào shì wǒ qù wǎn le nǐ men jiù xiān chī bú yào děng wǒ — If I’m late, go ahead and eat; don’t wait for me.

examples.text: 你要喜欢就多吃点儿。
examples.translation: nǐ yào xǐ huān jiù duō chī diǎnr — If you like it, eat more.

examples.text: 我要是会游泳就好了！
examples.translation: wǒ yào shì huì yóu yǒng jiù hǎo le — If only I could swim!

explanations.title: Activity 8 (Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: Pair up. David is considering quitting his part-time job. Translate David’s thoughts in Column A into Chinese and read them to your partner; your partner does the same for Column B. Take notes, discuss David’s dilemma and help him reach a reasonable decision. Column A: 1. If I had money, I would not have to work in that library. 2. If I did not work, I would have more time to study. 3. If I had more time to study, my grades would be better. Column B: 4. If I had better grades, I could go to a better college. 5. If I go to a better college, I could earn more money in the future. 6. I need money now. My translations:

examples.text: 要是我有钱，我就不用在那个图书馆工作了。
examples.translation: yào shì wǒ yǒu qián wǒ jiù bú yòng zài nà ge tú shū guǎn gōng zuò le — If I had money, I wouldn’t have to work in that library. (A1)

examples.text: 要是我不工作，我就有更多的时间学习。
examples.translation: yào shì wǒ bù gōng zuò wǒ jiù yǒu gèng duō de shí jiān xué xí — If I didn’t work, I would have more time to study. (A2)

examples.text: 要是我有更多的时间学习，我的成绩就会好一些。
examples.translation: yào shì wǒ yǒu gèng duō de shí jiān xué xí wǒ de chéng jì jiù huì hǎo yì xiē — If I had more time to study, my grades would be better. (A3)

examples.text: 要是我的成绩更好，我就可以上更好的大学。
examples.translation: yào shì wǒ de chéng jì gèng hǎo wǒ jiù kě yǐ shàng gèng hǎo de dà xué — If my grades were better, I could go to a better college. (B4)

examples.text: 要是我上更好的大学，将来就能赚更多的钱。
examples.translation: yào shì wǒ shàng gèng hǎo de dà xué jiāng lái jiù néng zhuàn gèng duō de qián — If I go to a better college, I could earn more money in the future. (B5)

examples.text: 我现在需要钱。
examples.translation: wǒ xiàn zài xū yào qián — I need money now. (B6)

explanations.title: Activity 9 (Reading): 挤牛奶的女孩
explanations.body: A. Read the story (the picture is not included); note any unknown words and guess their meanings. B. Pair up; choose the three unknown words you think are most critical for understanding the story and verify with your partner. C. Complete the sentence “要是能和这样的人结婚，我就……” and share it with the class. My completion: 要是能和这样的人结婚，我就有一个幸福的家了。

examples.text: 一个女孩走在路上，她的手里提着一桶牛奶，看起来很高兴的样子。昨天晚上，她做了一个梦，梦到自己挤了很多很多的牛奶，卖了很多很多的钱。女孩一边走一边想，这个梦要是真的就好了。她又想，如果我真有那么多钱，我应该买些什么呢？对了！我要给自己买一条漂亮的新裙子。我要是穿上漂亮的裙子，就可以和别的女孩一样去参加舞会。我要是去参加舞会的话，就可能会认识一个又帅又有钱的男孩。要是他爱上我，我们就结婚！要是能和这样的人结婚，我就……就在这时，唉，可怜的女孩！她手里的桶掉到地上，牛奶洒了一地。
examples.translation: yí gè nǚ hái zǒu zài lù shàng tā de shǒu lǐ tí zhe yì tǒng niú nǎi kàn qǐ lái hěn gāo xìng de yàng zi zuó tiān wǎn shàng tā zuò le yí gè mèng mèng dào zì jǐ jǐ le hěn duō hěn duō de niú nǎi mài le hěn duō hěn duō de qián nǚ hái yì biān zǒu yì biān xiǎng zhè ge mèng yào shì zhēn de jiù hǎo le tā yòu xiǎng rú guǒ wǒ zhēn yǒu nà me duō qián wǒ yīng gāi mǎi xiē shén me ne duì le wǒ yào gěi zì jǐ mǎi yì tiáo piào liàng de xīn qún zi wǒ yào shì chuān shàng piào liàng de qún zi jiù kě yǐ hé bié de nǚ hái yí yàng qù cān jiā wǔ huì wǒ yào shì qù cān jiā wǔ huì de huà jiù kě néng huì rèn shí yí gè yòu shuài yòu yǒu qián de nán hái yào shì tā ài shàng wǒ wǒ men jiù jié hūn yào shì néng hé zhè yàng de rén jié hūn wǒ jiù jiù zài zhè shí āi kě lián de nǚ hái tā shǒu lǐ de tǒng diào dào dì shàng niú nǎi sǎ le yí dì — A girl is walking on the road, carrying a bucket of milk in her hand, looking very happy. Last night she had a dream: she dreamed that she milked a great deal of milk and sold it for a great deal of money. As she walked she thought, “If only this dream were true!” She also thought, “If I really had that much money, what should I buy? Oh yes! I’ll buy myself a pretty new dress. If I wear a pretty dress, I can go to the dance like other girls. If I go to the dance, I might meet a handsome and rich boy. If he falls in love with me, we’ll get married! If I can marry such a person, I will… will…” Just then, alas, poor girl! The bucket in her hand fell to the ground and the milk spilled all over.

examples.text: 要是能和这样的人结婚，我就有一个幸福的家了。
examples.translation: yào shì néng hé zhè yàng de rén jié hūn wǒ jiù yǒu yí gè xìng fú de jiā le — If I could marry such a person, I would have a happy home. (my completion)

exercises.prompt: Where can the subject of the result clause go?

options: 要是天气不好，我们就不去海边。
天气不好的话，我们就不去海边。
天气要是不好，我们就不去海边。
要是天气不好，就我们不去海边。
exercises.explanation: The result subject cannot follow 就.

exercises.prompt: What does 要是…就好了！ express?
What does 的话 do at the end of a conditional clause?
What does 你要喜欢就多吃点儿 mean?
options: If you like it, eat more
If you eat, you will like it
Don’t eat if you like it

exercises.prompt: What does 我要是会游泳就好了！ mean?
What did the girl dream about?
options: Milking a lot of milk and selling it for lots of money
exercises.explanation: 梦到自己挤了很多很多的牛奶，卖了很多很多的钱。

exercises.prompt: What did she plan to buy first?
exercises.explanation: 我要给自己买一条漂亮的新裙子。

exercises.prompt: What happened at the end of the story?
options: The bucket fell and the milk spilled

exercises.prompt: 要是我有钱，我___不用在那个图书馆工作了。
要是有钱的___，我就去很多国家旅行。
我要是早十分钟出门，就不会___机了！

lessons.title: 334. Lesson 13 Presentation 3: skill integration
lessons.subtitle: 索提亚送我 · 小刀 · 农场的公牛 · 王先生错过航班

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Listen to Dialog 1 and answer: 1. The passenger had to leave items behind at the security point; what are they? 2. What options did the passenger have with these items? 3. What did the passenger decide, and why? B. Listen to Dialog 2 and answer: 1. What does the security officer ask the passengers to do at the beginning? 2. What did the officer find in one passenger’s bag? 3. Why can’t this item be brought onto the plane? Pair up and compare. (Audio, not included.)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): at Munich airport
explanations.body: A. Read the passage; mark any unknown word and guess its meaning. B. Write three unknown words critical to your understanding; pair up and discuss their meanings, checking your dictionary for disagreements. C. Using the passage, listen to seven statements and mark each true or false (audio, not included).

examples.text: 离开德国的时候，我的朋友索提亚到慕尼黑机场送我。因为我的德语不太好，所以他和我一起去办理了登机手续，把行李也托运了。我跟他说了再见，然后自己去安检。没想到，我在这里遇到了麻烦。工作人员让我打开箱子检查。原来，里面有几把我在德国买的小刀。工作人员说，这样的东西只能托运，不能随身带上飞机。我想，那就只能在机场找一个邮局寄回国了。我离开了安检，可是不知道机场有没有邮局，而且飞机快起飞了。正在着急的时候，我看见索提亚向我走来！原来，他想看到我过了安检再走。我在安检处排了那么长时间的队他也没有离开。我赶紧把小刀都给了他，说：“留下一把你最喜欢的，剩下的寄给我！”回国以后不久，我就收到了从德国寄来的几把精美的小刀。
examples.translation: lí kāi dé guó de shí hòu wǒ de péng yǒu suǒ tí yà dào mù ní hēi jī chǎng sòng wǒ yīn wèi wǒ de dé yǔ bú tài hǎo suǒ yǐ tā hé wǒ yì qǐ qù bàn lǐ le dēng jī shǒu xù bǎ xíng li yě tuō yùn le wǒ gēn tā shuō le zài jiàn rán hòu zì jǐ qù ān jiǎn méi xiǎng dào wǒ zài zhè lǐ yù dào le má fán gōng zuò rén yuán ràng wǒ dǎ kāi xiāng zi jiǎn chá yuán lái lǐ miàn yǒu jǐ bǎ wǒ zài dé guó mǎi de xiǎo dāo gōng zuò rén yuán shuō zhè yàng de dōng xī zhǐ néng tuō yùn bù néng suí shēn dài shàng fēi jī wǒ xiǎng nà jiù zhǐ néng zài jī chǎng zhǎo yí gè yóu jú jì huí guó le wǒ lí kāi le ān jiǎn kě shì bù zhī dào jī chǎng yǒu méi yǒu yóu jú ér qiě fēi jī kuài qǐ fēi le zhèng zài zháo jí de shí hòu wǒ kàn jiàn suǒ tí yà xiàng wǒ zǒu lái yuán lái tā xiǎng kàn dào wǒ guò le ān jiǎn zài zǒu wǒ zài ān jiǎn chù pái le nà me cháng shí jiān de duì tā yě méi yǒu lí kāi wǒ gǎn jǐn bǎ xiǎo dāo dōu gěi le tā shuō liú xià yì bǎ nǐ zuì xǐ huān de shèng xià de jì gěi wǒ huí guó yǐ hòu bù jiǔ wǒ jiù shōu dào le cóng dé guó jì lái de jǐ bǎ jīng měi de xiǎo dāo — When I left Germany, my friend Sotiya came to Munich airport to see me off. Because my German isn’t very good, he went with me to check in and checked my luggage too. I said goodbye to him and then went to security by myself. Unexpectedly, I ran into trouble here. The staff asked me to open my suitcase for inspection. As it turned out, inside there were several knives I had bought in Germany. The staff said that such things can only be checked, not carried onto the plane. I thought, then I can only find a post office in the airport and mail them home. I left security, but I didn’t know whether the airport had a post office, and the plane was about to take off. While I was anxious, I saw Sotiya walking toward me! As it turned out, he had wanted to see me through security before leaving. He hadn’t left even though I had stood in line at security for so long. I hurried to give him all the knives and said: “Keep the one you like best and mail the rest to me!” Not long after I returned home, I received several exquisite knives mailed from Germany.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Listening, Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Listen to the passage; transcribe any unknown words you hear and look up their meanings (audio, not included). B. Answer the following questions, then pair up and discuss your answers in Chinese:

examples.text: “我”的工作是什么？
examples.translation: wǒ de gōng zuò shì shén me — What is the narrator’s job?

examples.text: “我”为什么那么晚才到机场？
examples.translation: wǒ wèi shén me nà me wǎn cái dào jī chǎng — Why did the narrator get to the airport so late?

examples.text: “我”是怎么办登机手续的？
examples.translation: wǒ shì zěn me bàn dēng jī shǒu xù de — How did the narrator check in?

examples.text: “我”有几件托运行李？几件随身带的行李？
examples.translation: wǒ yǒu jǐ jiàn tuō yùn xíng li jǐ jiàn suí shēn dài de xíng li — How many checked and carry-on pieces?

examples.text: 安检的地方排队的人多吗？
examples.translation: ān jiǎn de dì fāng pái duì de rén duō ma — Were there many people lining up at security?

examples.text: “我”在安检有什么麻烦吗？
examples.translation: wǒ zài ān jiǎn yǒu shén me má fán ma — Did the narrator have trouble at security?

examples.text: “我”的鞋子怎么了？
examples.translation: wǒ de xié zi zěn me le — What happened to the narrator’s shoes?

examples.text: 广播里说的是什么？
examples.translation: guǎng bō lǐ shuō de shì shén me — What did the announcement say?

examples.text: “我”有没有赶上飞机？
examples.translation: wǒ yǒu méi yǒu gǎn shàng fēi jī — Did the narrator catch the plane?

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Speaking and Listening): Story 1
explanations.body: A. Pair up. Each partner reads one of the two stories and answers the questions that follow. Story 1 questions: 1. Why does the young man want to take a short cut? 2. Where does the short cut go? 3. Will the young man take the short cut? Why? (Mine: 1. He is afraid he won’t catch the six o’clock train. 2. Through a path across a farm. 3. Probably not, because of the bull.)

examples.text: 一个年轻人一大早要去赶火车，因为怕时间来不及，他想走一条最短的路，就是农场的一条小路。他问农场的主人：“我可以从你的农场过一下吗？这样可以快一点儿，因为我要坐早上六点的火车。”农场主说：“当然可以！要是我农场里的公牛发现了你，就是早上五点的火车你都能赶上！”

Explain three critical words in your passage to your partner, then retell the story; let your partner answer the questions you did and compare.

examples.text: 王先生在生活小事上非常粗心。有一次他需要到美国去开会，他提前两个小时就到了机场，心里想，这次一定不会误机了。他轻松地走到航空公司的服务台边，说：“请给我办理登机手续。”值机员认真地看了看他的机票，说：“对不起，先生，您错过您的航班了。”他惊讶地说：“这不可能！飞机提前起飞了吗？”值机员说：“很抱歉。您的航班昨天就起飞了。”

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Why is the check-in gate closed before the departure time of the flight? Read this online post (from blog.sina.com.cn/ceayoung) and report to your partner. The book prints the numbers as digits (30, 100, 60, 90); they are spelled out here.

examples.text: 经常坐飞机的人都知道，乘坐飞机一定要在航班起飞前三十分钟办理登机手续。这是为什么呢？首先我们要知道，什么是起飞时间。起飞时间是飞机关机门的时间，而不是飞机离地升空的时间。在停止办理登机手续到关机门之间，机场的工作人员还有很多工作要做。比如：1. 把旅客托运的行李装上飞机，2. 对办完登机手续的旅客进行安全检查，3. 让旅客到指定的登机口检票登机，4. 检查飞机上旅客的人数，看和地面检票人数是不是一样。按规定，一百座以下的飞机要在起飞前六十分钟就开始办理登机手续，一百座以上的飞机要提前九十分钟开始办理登机手续。因此，请旅客们一定要提前到机场办理登机手续。办完登机手续以后，还要及时进行安全检查，并到登机口候机。
examples.translation: jīng cháng zuò fēi jī de rén dōu zhī dào chéng zuò fēi jī yí dìng yào zài háng bān qǐ fēi qián sān shí fēn zhōng bàn lǐ dēng jī shǒu xù zhè shì wèi shén me ne shǒu xiān wǒ men yào zhī dào shén me shì qǐ fēi shí jiān qǐ fēi shí jiān shì fēi jī guān jī mén de shí jiān ér bú shì fēi jī lí dì shēng kōng de shí jiān zài tíng zhǐ bàn lǐ dēng jī shǒu xù dào guān jī mén zhī jiān jī chǎng de gōng zuò rén yuán hái yǒu hěn duō gōng zuò yào zuò bǐ rú bǎ lǚ kè tuō yùn de xíng li zhuāng shàng fēi jī duì bàn wán dēng jī shǒu xù de lǚ kè jìn xíng ān quán jiǎn chá ràng lǚ kè dào zhǐ dìng de dēng jī kǒu jiǎn piào dēng jī jiǎn chá fēi jī shàng lǚ kè de rén shù kàn hé dì miàn jiǎn piào rén shù shì bú shì yí yàng àn guī dìng yì bǎi zuò yǐ xià de fēi jī yào zài qǐ fēi qián liù shí fēn zhōng jiù kāi shǐ bàn lǐ dēng jī shǒu xù yì bǎi zuò yǐ shàng de fēi jī yào tí qián jiǔ shí fēn zhōng kāi shǐ bàn lǐ dēng jī shǒu xù yīn cǐ qǐng lǚ kè men yí dìng yào tí qián dào jī chǎng bàn lǐ dēng jī shǒu xù bàn wán dēng jī shǒu xù yǐ hòu hái yào jí shí jìn xíng ān quán jiǎn chá bìng dào dēng jī kǒu hòu jī — Those who often fly know that to take a plane you must check in 30 minutes before the flight takes off. Why is that? First we need to know what the takeoff time is. The takeoff time is the time the plane’s door is closed, not the time the plane leaves the ground. Between the end of check-in and the closing of the door, airport staff still have a lot of work to do, for example: 1. load passengers’ checked luggage on the plane; 2. carry out security checks on passengers who have finished check-in; 3. have passengers check their tickets and board at the designated gate; 4. check the number of passengers on the plane against the number checked at the gate. By regulation, check-in for planes with fewer than 100 seats begins 60 minutes before takeoff, and for planes with more than 100 seats 90 minutes before takeoff. Therefore, passengers must arrive early at the airport to check in. After check-in you still must go through the security check in good time and wait at the boarding gate.

lessons.title: 337. Lesson 13 Area Studies: Beijing Daxing International Airport (PKX)
lessons.subtitle: 北京大兴国际机场 · 海星 · 凤凰 · 感应式通关

explanations.title: Beijing Daxing International Airport (PKX)
explanations.body: Beijing Daxing International Airport (PKX), also known as Beijing New Airport, is one of the largest airport terminals in the world. It is one of two international airports for Beijing, along with Beijing Capital International Airport. This new airport is located south of the Daxing District (the southern suburbs of Beijing). This new mega-airport hub is expected to handle up to 45 million passengers per year by 2021, and to reach an amazing 100 million passengers per year in the future. Daxing airport’s exotic shape has earned it the nickname “The Starfish.” It is of enormous dimensions with a vast terminal covering 700,000 m²; with a ground transportation center extending 80,000 m². Currently Daxing Airport has four runways and 79 aircraft terminals. Eventually the airport will have 7 runways and be able to serve over 620,000 flights per year.

rows: up to 45 million by 2021; 100 million in the future
700,000 square meters; ground transportation center 80,000 square meters
Maximum walk from the center to a gate
5 to 7 minutes; now no waiting for most passengers
tables.title: Key facts

explanations.title: Layout and design
explanations.body: Passengers can go to the central terminal, where all the shops and facilities are located, and then head to their departure gates, situated in one of the corridors. Despite the huge size of the airport, the walking distance between the center and each gate is short. Passengers can shop and wander around care-free, knowing that their gate is only 8 minutes away at maximum. For passengers with long layovers between flights, the airport has a hotel, lounges, restaurants and even a 24-hour fitness center. Daxing Airport’s design is inspired by Chinese tradition and culture. Typical Chinese touches are combined with futuristic elements. While five outdoor traditional Chinese gardens adorn the five corridors, the airport’s shape can be compared to a giant phoenix, a very characteristic Chinese symbol. (Photographs from cctv.com.cn are not included.)

explanations.title: Speed and smart services
explanations.body: At Daxing Airport, speed is the priority. 5-G based technology and smart services cut down on waiting time. Facial recognition procedures make paper tickets unnecessary and 400 self-service points make checking in a breeze. Self-service baggage processes also help to optimize the traveller’s experience. You can track your luggage with E-tag technology. Daxing Airport has built intelligent customs, or “inductive customs clearance” that serves passengers with no waiting time. In the past when entering the country, passengers had to form long lines to pick up luggage and then pass through a machine inspection. Customs clearance times could be as long as 5 to 7 minutes. At Daxing International Airport (except for a small number of key passengers and luggage that need to enter the inspection area for customs inspection) most passengers no longer need to carry their luggage or line up to go through machine inspection.

explanations.title: Combined inspection
explanations.body: The customs and the security inspection departments share the inspection site and combine both customs inspection of luggage and items with the security inspection process. In this way, two “checkpoints” for customs inspection and airport security are combined. Passengers only need to check in their baggage once when leaving the country and go through only one inspection. The waiting time for inspections can be reduced by 50%. When unpacking and inspection is required, the customs and security inspections use separate inspection rooms, which provide more complete protection for passengers’ privacy. References: Wikipedia, Beijing Daxing International Airport; CCTV, Newly Completed Daxing Airport from Inside.

explanations.title: Learning objectives and Getting Started
explanations.body: Lesson 14 Leisure Travel. After this lesson you can compare different modes of transportation, discuss travel plans (destinations, travel times, modes of travel) and describe your travel experiences. You must master: the new words, the experience marker 过, the preposition 离, the construction 从…到…, 什么 + 吗, the rhetorical question 反问句, 多 in exclamatory sentences, 还是 for preference, the time-measurement complement 时量补语, the double 了 structure and compound directional verbs. Getting Started. Pair up and discuss: A. How do you usually get around in Monterey? B. How do you get to class each day? C. What modes of transportation do you use when you travel, and why?

lessons.title: 340. Lesson 14 Presentation 1 grammar: the experience marker 过
lessons.subtitle: 我还没去过北海 · 我奶奶没坐过飞机 · 去过长城没有？

explanations.title: The Experience Marker 过
explanations.body: In Chinese, when the aspect particle 过 is used immediately after a verb, it indicates a past experience. It is like the meaning of “ever” in English. When 过 is used as an experience marker, it follows the verb and precedes the object if there is one. Its negative is formed with 没有 and its interrogative forms include both the 吗-question and the affirmative-negative patterns. Positive: Subject + Verb + 过 + Object. Negative: Subject + 没(有) + Verb + 过 + Object. Interrogative: Subject + Verb + 过 + Object + 吗？ / Subject + Verb + 过 + Object + 没有？ Example from the dialog: 来北京这么长时间，我还没去过北海呢。 (I have been in Beijing for so long; however, I haven’t been to Beihai Park yet.)

examples.text: 我去过日本。
examples.translation: wǒ qù guò rì běn — I have been to Japan.

examples.text: 来国防语言学院以前，大卫学过西班牙文。
examples.translation: lái guó fáng yǔ yán xué yuàn yǐ qián dà wèi xué guò xī bān yá wén — Before coming to the Defense Language Institute, David had studied Spanish.

examples.text: 我没有去过华盛顿。
examples.translation: wǒ méi yǒu qù guò huá shèng dùn — I haven’t been to Washington. (没（有） is optional.)

examples.text: 我奶奶没坐过飞机。
examples.translation: wǒ nǎi nǎi méi zuò guò fēi jī — My grandmother has never taken a plane.

examples.text: 你去过中国吗？
examples.translation: nǐ qù guò zhōng guó ma — Have you been to China?

examples.text: 我去过北京，也去过上海。
examples.translation: wǒ qù guò běi jīng yě qù guò shàng hǎi — I’ve been to Beijing and also to Shanghai.

examples.text: 你父母见过你的男朋友没有？
examples.translation: nǐ fù mǔ jiàn guò nǐ de nán péng yǒu méi yǒu — Have your parents met your boyfriend?

explanations.title: Experience marker 过 versus past tense 了
explanations.body: The “Verb + 过 + Object” pattern emphasizes that an event has been experienced at least once in the past. The “Verb + 了 + Object” pattern indicates that a specific action has taken place with reference to a specific point in time. If you ask a tourist if they have been to the Great Wall since they came to China, you use 过. If you want to ask a tourist if they went to the Great Wall as scheduled, you use 了.

examples.text: 你去过长城没有？
examples.translation: nǐ qù guò cháng chéng méi yǒu — Have you been to the Great Wall? (experience, 过)

examples.text: 你今天去了长城没有？
examples.translation: nǐ jīn tiān qù le cháng chéng méi yǒu — Did you go to the Great Wall today? (a specific scheduled event, 了)

examples.text: 我去过纽约。

examples.text: 去年夏天我去了纽约。
examples.translation: qù nián xià tiān wǒ qù le niǔ yuē — Last summer I went to New York. (a specific time, 了)
