explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context Activity 1 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 宅急便 (zháijíbiàn, delivery service; 宅 home, 急 hurry, 便 convenient), a term used often in Taiwan. A. Read the table from the popular express service 黑猫宅急便 website in Taiwan (the web address is not given here) and determine what services the company provides. B. Pair up and discuss your findings; then generate five questions to ask customer service. C. Call the customer service representative and get more details about their service; your partner plays the representative; then switch roles.

headers: 说明 (the book’s table from the 黑猫宅急便 website; the Latin parts are left out)
tables.title: 服务介绍 (Taiwan’s 黑猫宅急便; 宅急便 zháijíbiàn, delivery service: 宅 home, 急 hurry, 便 convenient)

explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context Activity 2 (Reading, Speaking and Listening): the FAQ
explanations.body: Read the following FAQ from an express service and help create a Do’s and Don’ts list for customers. A. Form groups of three. Each member picks two of the six FAQs, reads them and takes notes. B. Each member reports what they read, gathers the remaining information from the group and writes up a Do’s and Don’ts list for customers; post your work on Linoit. C. The entire class votes for the best list. The six questions and answers:

rows: 可以到代收店、营业点寄件，或打电话、上网、用手机预约；可以让家人或大楼管理员代收；可以让收件人付运费；寄件时选好收件时间
不要寄到邮政信箱；不要寄现金、动物、超大件家具、电视、冰箱、自行车、护照；不要寄到军营、军校；不能先把行李寄到机场
tables.title: Using Chinese in Context Activity 2 B: the Do and Don’t list (blank in the book; my fill from the six FAQs)

examples.text: 我要寄快递，怎么寄呢？
examples.translation: wǒ yào jì kuài dì zěn me jì ne — Q1. I want to send an express parcel; how do I send it?

examples.text: 您可以到我们的代收店，像是各地的七一一便利商店，或是我们各地的营业点寄件，您也可以直接打电话到客服专线四一二，八八八八，或网络客服和我们联系。另外，我们也提供网络预约和手机应用程序预约的服务。只要是一个星期内的寄件，服务人员会在您选择的收件日去您家收件。
examples.translation: nín kě yǐ dào wǒ men de dài shōu diàn xiàng shì gè dì de qī yī yī biàn lì shāng diàn huò shì wǒ men gè dì de yíng yè diǎn jì jiàn nín yě kě yǐ zhí jiē dǎ diàn huà dào kè fú zhuān xiàn sì yī èr bā bā bā bā huò wǎng luò kè fú hé wǒ men lián xì lìng wài wǒ men yě tí gōng wǎng luò yù yuē hé shǒu jī yìng yòng chéng xù yù yuē de fú wù zhǐ yào shì yí gè xīng qī nèi de jì jiàn fú wù rén yuán huì zài nín xuǎn zé de shōu jiàn rì qù nín jiā shōu jiàn — A1. You can go to our agent stores, such as 7-11 convenience stores everywhere, or to our business points to send; you can also call the customer service line 412-8888 directly or contact us through online customer service. In addition we offer online and mobile app booking. For any item sent within one week, service staff will come to your home on the pick-up day you choose. (the book prints this in mixed traditional and simplified characters, writes 7-11 and the number in digits, and “app” in Latin letters)

examples.text: 我白天都不在家，要怎么样才能收到包裹呢？
examples.translation: wǒ bái tiān dōu bú zài jiā yào zěn me yàng cái néng shōu dào bāo guǒ ne — Q2. I’m never home during the day; how can I receive the parcel?

examples.text: 我们的配送最晚到晚上六点，您可以请寄件人在寄件时勾选十四时到十八时的时间，或者您可以请家人或是大楼管理员代收。此外，如果收件地址填写您上班的地方，我们也一样都会帮您配送喔。
examples.translation: wǒ men de pèi sòng zuì wǎn dào wǎn shàng liù diǎn nín kě yǐ qǐng jì jiàn rén zài jì jiàn shí gōu xuǎn shí sì shí dào shí bā shí de shí jiān huò zhě nín kě yǐ qǐng jiā rén huò shì dà lóu guǎn lǐ yuán dài shōu cǐ wài rú guǒ shōu jiàn dì zhǐ tián xiě nín shàng bān de dì fāng wǒ men yě yí yàng dōu huì bāng nín pèi sòng ō — A2. Our delivery runs until six in the evening at the latest; you can ask the sender to tick the 14:00–18:00 slot when sending, or you can have family or the building manager receive it for you. Also, if you put your workplace as the delivery address, we will deliver there just the same.

examples.text: 我可以寄到邮政信箱吗？
examples.translation: wǒ kě yǐ jì dào yóu zhèng xìn xiāng ma — Q3. Can I send to a P.O. box?

examples.text: 很抱歉，由于包裹寄到邮政信箱后没有人可以签收，所以我们不能提供这个服务。另外，如军营、军校等地址我们也无法托运。
examples.translation: hěn bào qiàn yóu yú bāo guǒ jì dào yóu zhèng xìn xiāng hòu méi yǒu rén kě yǐ qiān shōu suǒ yǐ wǒ men bù néng tí gōng zhè ge fú wù lìng wài rú jūn yíng jūn xiào děng dì zhǐ wǒ men yě wú fǎ tuō yùn — A3. Sorry, because nobody can sign for a parcel sent to a P.O. box, we cannot provide this service. Also we cannot ship to addresses such as military camps and military schools.

examples.text: 什么东西你们不能寄送？
examples.translation: shén me dōng xī nǐ men bù néng jì sòng — Q4. What can’t you send?

examples.text: 现金、动物、超大件家具、电视、冰箱、自行车、护照等，我们不能帮您运送。
examples.translation: xiàn jīn dòng wù chāo dà jiàn jiā jù diàn shì bīng xiāng zì xíng chē hù zhào děng wǒ men bù néng bāng nín yùn sòng — A4. Cash, animals, oversized furniture, televisions, refrigerators, bicycles, passports and so on we cannot ship for you.

examples.text: 你们提供先把行李寄到机场，出国时再提领的服务吗？
examples.translation: nǐ men tí gōng xiān bǎ xíng li jì dào jī chǎng chū guó shí zài tí lǐng de fú wù ma — Q5. Do you offer a service of sending luggage to the airport first and picking it up when going abroad?

examples.text: 我们现在不提供这样的服务。
examples.translation: wǒ men xiàn zài bù tí gōng zhè yàng de fú wù — A5. We do not offer such a service now.

examples.text: 你们的运费可不可以请收件人给付？
examples.translation: nǐ men de yùn fèi kě bù kě yǐ qǐng shōu jiàn rén jǐ fù — Q6. Can the freight be paid by the recipient?

examples.text: 可以，您的运费可以让收件人付。包裹送到时，我们的工作人员会向收件人收取运费。
examples.translation: kě yǐ nín de yùn fèi kě yǐ ràng shōu jiàn rén fù bāo guǒ sòng dào shí wǒ men de gōng zuò rén yuán huì xiàng shōu jiàn rén shōu qǔ yùn fèi — A6. Yes, your freight can be paid by the recipient. When the parcel is delivered, our staff will collect the freight from the recipient.

explanations.title: Using Chinese in Context Activities 3 and 4
explanations.body: Activity 3 (Reading, Speaking and Listening): You are studying Chinese at Beijing University and would like to send a Chinese New Year present through EMS to your friend, who now lives in Shanghai. A. At the post office you are asked to fill out an EMS form; figure out what information needs to be provided and fill out the form in Chinese (a photograph of an EMS form, not included). B. Go to a counter in the post office and mail the package to your friend; a classmate plays the postal clerk. Activity 4 (Reading, Speaking and Listening): You are doing an internship at a U.S. company in Shanghai. Your company often needs to mail products domestically and internationally; to reduce costs while still ensuring parcels are delivered as quickly as possible, your manager wants your team to research the two biggest express services in China, 顺丰 and 申通, and compare their rates, services, delivery times and user friendliness. Prepare a PPT report for your manager and give an oral report. A. Form groups of three; use the two companies’ websites (links not included; 顺丰: 我要寄件, 运费时效查询, 快递服务; 申通: 运费查询, 产品服务). B. Discuss your findings and decide what to include in your slides. C. Deliver an oral report using your presentation. D. The entire class votes on which delivery company to recommend.

examples.text: 陈雪晴：您好，我有个包裹要寄到纽约。
examples.translation: chén xuě qíng nín hǎo wǒ yǒu gè bāo guǒ yào jì dào niǔ yuē — Hello, I have a parcel to send to New York.

examples.text: 营业员：你想怎么寄？我们有航空、海运，还有特快专递？
examples.translation: yíng yè yuán nǐ xiǎng zěn me jì wǒ men yǒu háng kōng hǎi yùn hái yǒu tè kuài zhuān dì — How do you want to send it? We have air, sea and express delivery.

examples.text: 陈雪晴：哪个最快？
examples.translation: chén xuě qíng nǎ ge zuì kuài — Which is fastest?

examples.text: 营业员：特快专递最快，最多五个工作日就到，但是价钱贵一些。空运、海运慢一点，但是价钱便宜很多。
examples.translation: yíng yè yuán tè kuài zhuān dì zuì kuài zuì duō wǔ gè gōng zuò rì jiù dào dàn shì jià qián guì yì xiē kōng yùn hǎi yùn màn yì diǎn dàn shì jià qián pián yi hěn duō — Express is fastest, it arrives in five working days at most, but the price is a bit higher. lessons.title: 504. Lesson 20 Presentation 2 grammar: the post-modifier cluster in the 比 pattern
lessons.subtitle: 高铁比特快车快得多 · 很多 多了 不少 一点儿 · 更 还 · 省略 B

explanations.title: Post-modifier cluster in 比 pattern
explanations.body: When used for comparison, the degree to modify the bare adjective needs to be placed after the adjective: A 比 B + adj. + post-modifier cluster (to indicate degree). The cluster can be 得多, 很多, 多了, 不少, 一点(儿), or a specific amount such as 2–3 个钟头. Occasionally the 比 “B” portion may be omitted because the context is known, but the sense of comparison is still implied. The adverbs 更 and 还 can be placed before the adjective when making a comparison.

rows: 得多 / 很多 / 多了 / 不少 / 一点(儿) / a specific amount such as 2–3 个钟头
tables.title: A 比 B + adj. + post-modifier cluster

examples.text: 高铁比特快车快得多。
examples.translation: gāo tiě bǐ tè kuài chē kuài de duō — The high-speed rail is much faster than the express train.

examples.text: 空运、海运慢一点，不过价钱便宜很多。

examples.text: 特快专递比航空包裹更快。

lessons.title: 505. Lesson 20 Presentation 2 grammar: 最多 and 最少
lessons.subtitle: 最多 = at most, 最少 = at least · 坐飞机还是坐高铁 · 两真一假

explanations.title: The usage of 最多 and 最少
explanations.body: 最多 indicates “maximum” and 最少 indicates “minimum.” These are generally placed after the subject and followed by a verb, number, measure word, or a noun. Sub + 最多 + verb + number + measure + noun. Sub + 最少 + verb + number + measure + noun. The book’s four examples, with the digits spelled out:

examples.text: 从中国寄快递包裹到纽约最多只要三个工作日。
examples.translation: cóng zhōng guó jì kuài dì bāo guǒ dào niǔ yuē zuì duō zhǐ yào sān gè gōng zuò rì — From China, sending an express parcel to New York takes only three working days at most. (the book writes 3)

examples.text: 从旧金山坐飞机到台北最少要十三个小时。
examples.translation: cóng jiù jīn shān zuò fēi jī dào tái běi zuì shǎo yào shí sān gè xiǎo shí — Flying from San Francisco to Taipei takes at least thirteen hours. (the book writes 13)

examples.text: 要通过语言能力考试，你最少要认识一千六百个汉字。
examples.translation: yào tōng guò yǔ yán néng lì kǎo shì nǐ zuì shǎo yào rèn shí yì qiān liù bǎi gè hàn zì — To pass the language proficiency test you need to know at least 1,600 characters. (the book writes “DLPT 考试” and 1600; I wrote the name in characters because these examples are spoken)

examples.text: 明天的生日派对，你最多需要准备十个人的饭菜。
examples.translation: míng tiān de shēng rì pài duì nǐ zuì duō xū yào zhǔn bèi shí gè rén de fàn cài — For tomorrow’s birthday party you need to prepare food for ten people at most. (the book writes 10)

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: Think about your past experiences. Create three statements about yourself using 最多 and 最少, with two statements that are false and one that is true. See if your classmates can guess which statement about you is true. The book’s examples, followed by the question 哪个不是真的？

examples.text: 我的银行账户最多只有两千块钱。
examples.translation: wǒ de yín háng zhàng hù zuì duō zhǐ yǒu liǎng qiān kuài qián — My bank account has two thousand yuan at most. (the book’s example, with 2000 spelled out)

examples.text: 我最多只能吃三碗饭。
examples.translation: wǒ zuì duō zhǐ néng chī sān wǎn fàn — I can eat three bowls of rice at most. (the book’s example)

examples.translation: wǒ zuì shǎo néng rèn de sān bǎi gè hàn zì — I can recognize at least three hundred characters. (the book’s example, with 300 spelled out)

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Read the following passage and take notes in the table about the aspects of air travel and high-speed rail. B. In Chinese, check your answer with your partner: Student A reports on the first column and Student B on the second. The passage:

rows: 为了安全，越来越花时间；最少提前一个小时到机场，办登机手续，通过安检；人多时最少排一个多小时的队
车站多半在城内，比较方便；速度快；很少晚点
飞行时间再加上两三个小时的交通和等候时间
从北京到上海最多不到五个小时
为旅客省下不少时间，所以越来越多的人选择高铁
tables.title: Activity 4A: notes on the passage (the book leaves the table blank; this is my filling)

examples.text: 近几年来由于安全的原因，坐飞机越来越花时间。如果是坐国内的航班，人们最少要提前一个小时到机场。到了机场以后，还要办登机手续和通过安检。人多的时候，有时最少要排上一个多小时的队。除了飞行时间，最少还要再加上两三个小时的交通时间和等候时间。所以现在有越来越多的人选择坐高铁，因为高铁站多半在城内，比较方便，而且速度快，从北京到上海最多不到五个小时。另外，列车也很少晚点。因此，可以为旅客省下不少时间。
examples.translation: jìn jǐ nián lái yóu yú ān quán de yuán yīn zuò fēi jī yuè lái yuè huā shí jiān rú guǒ shì zuò guó nèi de háng bān rén men zuì shǎo yào tí qián yí gè xiǎo shí dào jī chǎng dào le jī chǎng yǐ hòu hái yào bàn dēng jī shǒu xù hé tōng guò ān jiǎn rén duō de shí hòu yǒu shí zuì shǎo yào pái shàng yí gè duō xiǎo shí de duì chú le fēi xíng shí jiān zuì shǎo hái yào zài jiā shàng liǎng sān gè xiǎo shí de jiāo tōng shí jiān hé děng hòu shí jiān suǒ yǐ xiàn zài yǒu yuè lái yuè duō de rén xuǎn zé zuò gāo tiě yīn wèi gāo tiě zhàn duō bàn zài chéng nèi bǐ jiào fāng biàn ér qiě sù dù kuài cóng běi jīng dào shàng hǎi zuì duō bú dào wǔ gè xiǎo shí lìng wài liè chē yě hěn shǎo wǎn diǎn yīn cǐ kě yǐ wèi lǚ kè shěng xià bù shǎo shí jiān — In recent years, for safety reasons, flying takes more and more time. For a domestic flight people have to arrive at the airport at least an hour ahead. After arriving they still have to check in and go through security. When there are many people, sometimes they have to queue for at least an hour or more. Besides the flying time, at least two or three more hours of transport and waiting time must be added. So now more and more people choose the high-speed rail, because the stations are mostly inside the city, which is more convenient, and it is fast: from Beijing to Shanghai it takes less than five hours at most. In addition, trains are seldom late. Therefore it can save travelers quite a lot of time. (the book prints digits and the typo 等侯; I wrote the numbers in characters and 等候)

lessons.title: 506. Lesson 20 Presentation 2 grammar: 要看 and 得看 (it depends)
lessons.subtitle: 那得看你保多少了 · 那要看我女朋友了 · 要看孩子的兴趣

explanations.title: The use of 要看
explanations.body: 要看 and 得看 are colloquial expressions, meaning “it depends (on).” They can be followed by a pronoun, a phrase or a sentence. In conversation, 这/那 is often placed before 要看 and 得看 to refer to the unknown outcome or topic previously discussed. In a statement, an unknown outcome can be used as a subject followed by 要看 or 得看 and an unclear situation. Pattern 1: (这/那) + 要看/得看 + unclear situation + 了 (examples 1–3). Pattern 2: unknown outcome + 要看/得看 + unclear situation (examples 4–5). Here 得 in 得看 is read děi.

examples.text: 保险费是多少？
examples.translation: bǎo xiǎn fèi shì duō shǎo — A: How much is the insurance?

examples.text: 那得看你保多少了。
examples.translation: nà děi kàn nǐ bǎo duō shǎo le — B: That depends on how much you insure it for.

examples.text: 你明天参不参加聚会？
examples.translation: nǐ míng tiān cān bù cān jiā jù huì — A: Are you going to the party tomorrow?

examples.text: 那要看我女朋友了。
examples.translation: nà yào kàn wǒ nǚ péng yǒu le — B: That depends on my girlfriend.

examples.text: 老师，我能不能通过语言能力考试？
examples.translation: lǎo shī wǒ néng bù néng tōng guò yǔ yán néng lì kǎo shì — A: Teacher, can I pass the language proficiency test? (the book writes DLPT)

examples.text: 那得看你学习够不够努力了。
examples.translation: nà děi kàn nǐ xué xí gòu bú gòu nǔ lì le — B: That depends on whether you study hard enough.

examples.text: 学不学音乐要看孩子的兴趣。
examples.translation: xué bù xué yīn yuè yào kàn hái zi de xìng qù — 4. Whether to learn music depends on the child’s interest.

examples.text: 能不能留在美国得看我能不能拿到签证。
examples.translation: néng bù néng liú zài měi guó děi kàn wǒ néng bù néng ná dào qiān zhèng — 5. Whether I can stay in the U.S. depends on whether I can get a visa.

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A new student from another class has struggled with life at DLI and in Monterey. Answer his questions by providing suggestions using 要看 or 得看. Pair up: Student A asks the questions and Student B offers suggestions; the students switch roles and take notes. The book lists six questions and two blank lines for your own questions; my suggested answers (the book prints none):

examples.text: 甲：我什么时候练习听力最好？

examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ yīng gāi zěn me jì shēng cí — Question: How should I memorize new words?

examples.text: 乙：那得看你习惯怎么学了。
examples.translation: yǐ nà děi kàn nǐ xí guàn zěn me xué le — Answer: That depends on how you are used to studying. (mine)

examples.text: 甲：我的学习这么紧张，周末我应该出去玩吗？
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ de xué xí zhè me jǐn zhāng zhōu mò wǒ yīng gāi chū qù wán ma — Question: My studies are so intense: should I go out and play on the weekend?

examples.text: 乙：那要看你的作业做完了没有。
examples.translation: yǐ nà yào kàn nǐ de zuò yè zuò wán le méi yǒu — Answer: That depends on whether you have finished your homework. (mine)

examples.text: 甲：我怎么样才能通过我的单元考试？
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ zěn me yàng cái néng tōng guò wǒ de dān yuán kǎo shì — Question: How can I pass my unit test?

examples.text: 乙：那要看你学习够不够努力了。
examples.translation: yǐ nà yào kàn nǐ xué xí gòu bú gòu nǔ lì le — Answer: That depends on whether you study hard enough. (mine)

examples.text: 甲：我应不应该在这里找个女朋友/男朋友？
examples.translation: jiǎ wǒ yīng bù yīng gāi zài zhè lǐ zhǎo gè nǚ péng yǒu nán péng yǒu — Question: Should I find a girlfriend/boyfriend here?

examples.text: 乙：这得看你有没有时间了。
examples.translation: yǐ zhè děi kàn nǐ yǒu méi yǒu shí jiān le — Answer: That depends on whether you have the time. (mine)

examples.text: 甲：周末的时候，在蒙特雷做什么活动最好？
examples.translation: jiǎ zhōu mò de shí hòu zài méng tè léi zuò shén me huó dòng zuì hǎo — Question: What is the best activity to do on weekends in Monterey?

examples.text: 乙：那要看你喜欢什么了。
examples.translation: yǐ nà yào kàn nǐ xǐ huān shén me le — Answer: That depends on what you like. (mine)

lessons.title: 507. Lesson 20 Presentation 2 grammar: 不过, 但是 and 可是
lessons.subtitle: 三个“但是” · 语气的轻重 · 配对练习

explanations.title: The use of 不过、但是 and 可是
explanations.body: 不过, 但是 and 可是 are similar in meaning, indicating “but,” “nevertheless,” or “however” and are often used interchangeably. However, 不过 has a softer tone, while 但是 and 可是 express stronger tones, with 但是 being more formal and 可是 more colloquial.

tables.title: 不过 · 可是 · 但是 (the book’s table)

examples.text: 特快专递最快，但是价钱有点儿贵。
examples.translation: tè kuài zhuān dì zuì kuài dàn shì jià qián yǒu diǎnr guì — Express is fastest, but the price is a little high.

examples.text: 空运、海运慢一点，不过价钱便宜很多。
examples.translation: kōng yùn hǎi yùn màn yì diǎn bú guò jià qián pián yi hěn duō — Air and sea are a little slower, but the price is much cheaper.

examples.text: 我很喜欢学中文，不过汉字很难学。
examples.translation: wǒ hěn xǐ huān xué zhōng wén bú guò hàn zì hěn nán xué — I like studying Chinese, but characters are hard to learn.

examples.text: 我想去听这场音乐会，可是我买不到票。
examples.translation: wǒ xiǎng qù tīng zhè chǎng yīn yuè huì kě shì wǒ mǎi bú dào piào — I want to go to this concert, but I can’t get a ticket.

explanations.title: Activity 6 (Listening, Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Listen to the first part of each sentence and match it with the appropriate ending by writing its letter in the parentheses. The book prints the seven endings (a to g) and the first halves are only on the audio (not included), so I wrote one first half for each ending as my own reconstruction. B. Pair up and check your answers by reading them aloud and translating the entire sentence; the book leaves seven lines for the translations. The seven endings as printed:

examples.text: 但是加上去机场和安检的时间，和坐高铁差不多。
examples.translation: dàn shì jiā shàng qù jī chǎng hé ān jiǎn de shí jiān hé zuò gāo tiě chà bu duō — a. But adding the time to go to the airport and through security, it is about the same as taking the high-speed rail.

examples.text: 可是厨具很全，冰箱、洗碗机都有。
examples.translation: kě shì chú jù hěn quán bīng xiāng xǐ wǎn jī dōu yǒu — b. But the kitchen equipment is complete, there is a refrigerator and a dishwasher.

examples.text: 可是不管输赢，他都很开心。

examples.text: 可是有各种各样的海洋动物。

lessons.title: 508. Lesson 20 Presentation 2 skill integration: postal rates, a missing parcel, mailing in America
lessons.subtitle: 平信 邮政编码 挂号信 回执 · 邮资表 · 特快专递没收到 · 小丽在美国邮局

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Speaking and Reading)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 平信 (píngxìn; surface/first class mail), 邮政编码 (yóuzhèng biānmǎ; zip code). A. Listen to the following sentences twice and answer: 1. What did the clerk say? 2. What was being explained? 3. What question was asked? 4. What did the man say? 5. What was said about the letter? 6. What did the customer ask for? B. Pair up and, in Chinese, share your answers with your partner. (Audio, not included; the book prints no script.)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Listening, Speaking and Reading)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 挂号信 (guàhào xìn; registered mail). A. Pair up. Student A listens to Dialog 1 and Student B listens to Dialog 2; each writes a summary and at least four details. B. Students share their information in Chinese and their partner fills in the other column. C. Students read the script and check their answers. (Audio and a script that this text does not print, so nothing to include.)

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Listening, Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 回执 (huí zhí; return receipt). A. Listen to the following conversation and mark each statement True or False; explain your choices in Chinese. The audio is not included and the book prints no key, so I give the six statements without an answer key. B. Pair up. You are in Beijing and want to mail several letters to your friends before Christmas. Check the postal rates below and carry out a conversation with a postal clerk; your partner plays the postal clerk. The statements, then the rates, then a sample conversation of mine:

rows: (none printed: one ¥1.5 value is shown for the city)
tables.title: Activity 3B: the postal rates in yuan (the + rows for 挂号信 and 回执 are added to the postage)

examples.text: 刘国华想往上海寄一封航空挂号信。

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. Read the passage about a customer’s experience at the post office and answer: 1. Provide at least two details. 2. What happened to the package? 3. What information was provided by the postal clerk during the customer’s second visit? 4. What was the customer instructed to do? B. Pair up and create a skit of a conversation between the postal clerk and the customer on his second visit (the book leaves lines for A and B, seven each). C. Present your skit to the class. The passage, then my skit:

examples.text: 上个星期我到邮局寄了一个特快专递的包裹给我女朋友。邮局的营业员告诉我，特快专递最快，最多只要三个工作日。因为这个礼物有些贵重，我还买了保险，一共花了五十六块钱。今天是我女朋友的生日，我给她打电话，祝她生日快乐，才知道她还没收到我的包裹。打完电话，我马上去邮局。邮局的营业员让我给他看那天的收据，然后问我有没有按照上面的二维码查包裹是不是已经寄到了。我告诉他网上说寄到了，但是我的女朋友没收到。他用电脑又帮我查了一遍，告诉我东西应该已经寄到了，因为包裹一送到寄件地址，邮差就扫码通知邮局了。他让我再问问女友或她的家人，看是不是她的家人已经帮她领了或者邮差留了一张条子通知她去邮局领。
examples.translation: shàng gè xīng qī wǒ dào yóu jú jì le yí gè tè kuài zhuān dì de bāo guǒ gěi wǒ nǚ péng yǒu yóu jú de yíng yè yuán gào sù wǒ tè kuài zhuān dì zuì kuài zuì duō zhǐ yào sān gè gōng zuò rì yīn wèi zhè ge lǐ wù yǒu xiē guì zhòng wǒ hái mǎi le bǎo xiǎn yí gòng huā le wǔ shí liù kuài qián jīn tiān shì wǒ nǚ péng yǒu de shēng rì wǒ gěi tā dǎ diàn huà zhù tā shēng rì kuài lè cái zhī dào tā hái méi shōu dào wǒ de bāo guǒ dǎ wán diàn huà wǒ mǎ shàng qù yóu jú yóu jú de yíng yè yuán ràng wǒ gěi tā kàn nà tiān de shōu jù rán hòu wèn wǒ yǒu méi yǒu àn zhào shàng miàn de èr wéi mǎ chá bāo guǒ shì bú shì yǐ jīng jì dào le wǒ gào sù tā wǎng shàng shuō jì dào le dàn shì wǒ de nǚ péng yǒu méi shōu dào tā yòng diàn nǎo yòu bāng wǒ chá le yí biàn gào sù wǒ dōng xī yīng gāi yǐ jīng jì dào le yīn wèi bāo guǒ yí sòng dào jì jiàn dì zhǐ yóu chāi jiù sǎo mǎ tōng zhī yóu jú le tā ràng wǒ zài wèn wèn nǚ yǒu huò tā de jiā rén kàn shì bú shì tā de jiā rén yǐ jīng bāng tā lǐng le huò zhě yóu chāi liú le yì zhāng tiáo zi tōng zhī tā qù yóu jú lǐng — Last week I went to the post office and mailed an express parcel to my girlfriend. The clerk told me express is fastest, only three working days at most. Because the gift is somewhat valuable I also bought insurance; it cost 56 yuan altogether. Today is my girlfriend’s birthday; I phoned her to wish her a happy birthday and only then learned that she had not received my parcel yet. After the call I went straight to the post office. The clerk asked me to show him the receipt from that day and then asked whether I had used the QR code on it to check whether the parcel had arrived. I told him the web said it had arrived but my girlfriend hadn’t received it. He checked again on the computer and told me the item should already have been delivered, because as soon as a parcel reaches the delivery address the postman scans the code and notifies the post office. He told me to ask my girlfriend or her family again, to see whether her family had already collected it for her or the postman had left a note telling her to collect it at the post office. (the book prints 3 and 56 as digits)

examples.text: 顾客：您好，我上个星期寄了一个特快专递，可是我女朋友还没收到。
examples.translation: gù kè nín hǎo wǒ shàng gè xīng qī jì le yí gè tè kuài zhuān dì kě shì wǒ nǚ péng yǒu hái méi shōu dào — Hello, I mailed an express parcel last week but my girlfriend still hasn’t received it. (skit mine)

examples.text: 营业员：请把那天的收据给我看一下。你按收据上的二维码查过没有？
examples.translation: yíng yè yuán qǐng bǎ nà tiān de shōu jù gěi wǒ kàn yí xià nǐ àn shōu jù shàng de èr wéi mǎ chá guò méi yǒu — Please show me that day’s receipt. Have you checked with the QR code on it? (mine)

examples.text: 顾客：查过了。网上说寄到了，可是我女朋友没收到。
examples.translation: gù kè chá guò le wǎng shàng shuō jì dào le kě shì wǒ nǚ péng yǒu méi shōu dào — I have. The web says it arrived, but my girlfriend didn’t receive it. (mine)

examples.text: 营业员：我用电脑再帮你查一遍。……东西应该已经寄到了，邮差一送到就扫码通知我们了。
examples.translation: yíng yè yuán wǒ yòng diàn nǎo zài bāng nǐ chá yí biàn dōng xī yīng gāi yǐ jīng jì dào le yóu chāi yí sòng dào jiù sǎo mǎ tōng zhī wǒ men le — Let me check again on the computer… The item should have arrived; the postman scans the code to notify us as soon as he delivers. (mine)

examples.text: 顾客：那怎么办呢？
examples.translation: gù kè nà zěn me bàn ne — Then what should I do? (mine)

examples.text: 营业员：你再问问你女朋友或她的家人，看是不是家人已经帮她领了，或者邮差留了一张条子，通知她来邮局领。
examples.translation: yíng yè yuán nǐ zài wèn wèn nǐ nǚ péng yǒu huò tā de jiā rén kàn shì bú shì jiā rén yǐ jīng bāng tā lǐng le huò zhě yóu chāi liú le yì zhāng tiáo zi tōng zhī tā lái yóu jú lǐng — Ask your girlfriend or her family again to see whether the family collected it for her, or whether the postman left a note telling her to collect it at the post office. (mine)

examples.text: 顾客：好，谢谢您。我马上给她打电话。
examples.translation: gù kè hǎo xiè xiè nín wǒ mǎ shàng gěi tā dǎ diàn huà — OK, thank you. I’ll call her right away. (mine)

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading, Writing and Speaking)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 头疼 (tóuténg; headache). A. Below is a blogger’s post regarding the U.S. postal service. Read the passage and create a mind map to summarize the post. The book asks “What is his suggestion?” (the blogger is 小丽, so I treat it as “her”). B. Use the mind map to share the information with your partner in Chinese. My mind map in words: the center is “去美国邮局寄东西”; the branches are 1. 直接放进投递箱 (stamps enough, not overweight; also for returns of online purchases), 2. 去邮局排队请营业员帮忙 (they weigh and tell you how to send), 3. 用邮局门口的自动柜员机 (follow the screen); her suggestion is to ask the clerk. The passage:

examples.text: 我是小丽，是纽约大学的中国留学生。今天想跟大家说说我去美国邮局的经验。在国内我们都是用网路联系，几乎很少有人去邮局寄信。可是在美国，许多重要的文件还是得靠邮局寄送，所以到邮局寄信也几乎是留学生一定会有的体验。还记得第一次到邮局寄东西，邮局里的牌子上写着各种不同的寄信方式和计费方式，让我非常头疼。在美国，一共有三种寄件方式，如果已经贴了足够的邮费，而且信件或包裹没有超重就可直接放进邮局的投递箱里。很多人网购以后想要退东西，也是直接把包裹放进投递箱里。第二种寄件方式是，如果不知道该用哪种方式邮寄，也不知道是不是贴够了邮票，那就得直接去邮局，排队请邮局的工作人员帮助你，他们会帮你称重，然后告诉你可以怎么寄。第三种是使用邮局门口的自动柜员机，按照显示屏上一步一步去做就可以完成寄送手续。我觉得最简单的办法就是花一点时间问问邮局的营业员。这样，你就能找到比较适合你的邮寄选择。
examples.translation: wǒ shì xiǎo lì shì niǔ yuē dà xué de zhōng guó liú xué shēng jīn tiān xiǎng gēn dà jiā shuō shuō wǒ qù měi guó yóu jú de jīng yàn zài guó nèi wǒ men dōu shì yòng wǎng lù lián xì jī hū hěn shǎo yǒu rén qù yóu jú jì xìn kě shì zài měi guó xǔ duō zhòng yào de wén jiàn hái shì děi kào yóu jú jì sòng suǒ yǐ dào yóu jú jì xìn yě jī hū shì liú xué shēng yí dìng huì yǒu de tǐ yàn hái jì de dì yī cì dào yóu jú jì dōng xī yóu jú lǐ de pái zi shàng xiě zhe gè zhǒng bù tóng de jì xìn fāng shì hé jì fèi fāng shì ràng wǒ fēi cháng tóu téng zài měi guó yí gòng yǒu sān zhǒng jì jiàn fāng shì rú guǒ yǐ jīng tiē le zú gòu de yóu fèi ér qiě xìn jiàn huò bāo guǒ méi yǒu chāo zhòng jiù kě zhí jiē fàng jìn yóu jú de tóu dì xiāng lǐ hěn duō rén wǎng gòu yǐ hòu xiǎng yào tuì dōng xī yě shì zhí jiē bǎ bāo guǒ fàng jìn tóu dì xiāng lǐ dì èr zhǒng jì jiàn fāng shì shì rú guǒ bù zhī dào gāi yòng nǎ zhǒng fāng shì yóu jì yě bù zhī dào shì bú shì tiē gòu le yóu piào nà jiù děi zhí jiē qù yóu jú pái duì qǐng yóu jú de gōng zuò rén yuán bāng zhù nǐ tā men huì bāng nǐ chēng zhòng rán hòu gào sù nǐ kě yǐ zěn me jì dì sān zhǒng shì shǐ yòng yóu jú mén kǒu de zì dòng guì yuán jī àn zhào xiǎn shì píng shàng yí bù yí bù qù zuò jiù kě yǐ wán chéng jì sòng shǒu xù wǒ jué de zuì jiǎn dān de bàn fǎ jiù shì huā yì diǎn shí jiān wèn wèn yóu jú de yíng yè yuán zhè yàng nǐ jiù néng zhǎo dào bǐ jiào shì hé nǐ de yóu jì xuǎn zé — I am Xiaoli, a Chinese student studying at New York University. Today I’d like to tell everyone about my experience at the American post office. In China we all keep in touch over the internet and almost nobody goes to the post office to send letters. But in America many important documents still have to be sent through the post office, so mailing a letter at the post office is almost an experience every international student will have. I still remember the first time I went to mail something: the signs in the post office listed all kinds of different ways of sending and ways of charging, which gave me a big headache. In America there are three ways of sending. If you have already put on enough postage and the letter or parcel is not overweight, you can put it straight into the post office’s drop box. Many people who want to return something bought online also put the parcel directly into the drop box. The second way is that if you don’t know which method to use, and don’t know whether you have put on enough stamps, then you must go straight to the post office, queue, and ask the staff to help you; they will weigh it for you and tell you how you can send it. The third is to use the self-service machine at the post office door and complete the mailing by following the screen step by step. I think the simplest way is to spend a little time asking the clerk at the post office. That way you will find the mailing choice that suits you best.

exercises.prompt: According to the rate table, how much is ordinary mail to the U.S.?
According to the table, how much is airmail to Japan and Korea?
In the express-parcel story, why did the customer buy insurance?

options: He phoned his girlfriend on her birthday
exercises.explanation: 给她打电话…才知道她还没收到.

exercises.prompt: What did the clerk say about delivery?

The parcel is still in the plane

options: Ask his girlfriend or her family again, and look for the postman’s note

lessons.title: 509. Lesson 20 Presentation 2 using Chinese in context: at the post office and addressing envelopes
lessons.subtitle: 十个常用句 · 顾客和营业员 · 台湾的信封 · 台湾和美国的邮局

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: A. You are in China and need to mail a package and several letters. Pair up and think of how to say these in Chinese: 1. What would you say to the clerk if you want to mail a letter or package to the U.S.? 2. What would you ask if you wanted to know your mailing options? 3. How do the options differ (first class, air mail, registered mail, express mail)? 4. How much postage is needed to mail a letter to New York? 5. What would you say if you needed to purchase five 80-cent stamps and two 2.8-yuan stamps? 6. How much more does a special express package cost than an ordinary package? 7. Say that mailing a special express package costs much more than an ordinary one. 8. About how long does it take a letter or package to travel to the U.S. by air? 9. Can you write addresses on packages in English? 10. Tell the clerk you can’t write Chinese well and ask him to look and see whether you have correctly filled in the necessary form. My sentences (the book prints none):

examples.text: 你好，我想寄一封信到美国。
examples.translation: nǐ hǎo wǒ xiǎng jì yì fēng xìn dào měi guó — 1. Hello, I’d like to mail a letter to the U.S. (my sentence; the book asks for your own)

examples.text: 请问，你们有哪几种邮寄方式？
examples.translation: qǐng wèn nǐ men yǒu nǎ jǐ zhǒng yóu jì fāng shì — 2. Excuse me, which mailing methods do you have? (mine)

examples.text: 平信、航空信、挂号信和特快专递有什么不一样？
examples.translation: píng xìn háng kōng xìn guà hào xìn hé tè kuài zhuān dì yǒu shén me bù yí yàng — 3. How do ordinary mail, airmail, registered mail and express differ? (mine)

examples.text: 寄一封信到纽约，需要多少邮费？
examples.translation: jì yì fēng xìn dào niǔ yuē xū yào duō shǎo yóu fèi — 4. How much postage is needed to mail a letter to New York? (mine)

examples.text: 我要买五张八毛的邮票和两张两块八的邮票。
examples.translation: wǒ yào mǎi wǔ zhāng bā máo de yóu piào hé liǎng zhāng liǎng kuài bā de yóu piào — 5. I’d like five 80-cent stamps and two 2.8-yuan stamps. (mine; the book writes 80 and 2.8)

examples.text: 寄特快专递的包裹比寄普通的包裹贵多少？
examples.translation: jì tè kuài zhuān dì de bāo guǒ bǐ jì pǔ tōng de bāo guǒ guì duō shǎo — 6. How much more does it cost to mail an express parcel than an ordinary one? (mine)

examples.text: 寄特快专递的包裹比寄普通的包裹贵得多。
examples.translation: jì tè kuài zhuān dì de bāo guǒ bǐ jì pǔ tōng de bāo guǒ guì de duō — 7. Mailing an express parcel costs much more than an ordinary one. (mine)

examples.text: 空运寄一封信或者一个包裹到美国，大概要几天？
examples.translation: kōng yùn jì yì fēng xìn huò zhě yí gè bāo guǒ dào měi guó dà gài yào jǐ tiān — 8. About how many days does it take to send a letter or parcel to the U.S. by air? (mine)

examples.text: 包裹单上的地址可以用英文写吗？
examples.translation: bāo guǒ dān shàng de dì zhǐ kě yǐ yòng yīng wén xiě ma — 9. Can the address on the parcel form be written in English? (mine)

examples.text: 我的中文写得不太好，请你看看我填得对不对。
examples.translation: wǒ de zhōng wén xiě de bú tài hǎo qǐng nǐ kàn kàn wǒ tián de duì bú duì — 10. My Chinese writing isn’t very good; please look and see whether I filled it in correctly. (mine)

explanations.title: Activity 1B (role play)
explanations.body: Now you are at the post office in China and need to mail these letters and a package; consult with the post office clerk, played by your partner, then switch roles. A customer needs to ask: the mailing options; the price differences of different options; the time that it takes for the letter to reach the recipient; if the letter is overweight; how much postage you need to pay (surface, airmail, registered or express); if the package form is correctly filled; if you can track your package and how to do it. A postal clerk needs to ask or explain: different mailing options; the content of the package; how the customer must fill out various forms; if the customer wants to purchase insurance; if the customer wants a return receipt; if the customer wants additional services; how the customer wants to pay; the tracking information.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading, Speaking and Listening)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 邮递区号 (yóu dì qū hào; postal code), a term often used in Taiwan. Below are instructions on how to fill out a formal vertical envelope for domestic mail and a horizontal-style envelope for international mail in Taiwan. A. Pair up. Student A reads Scenario 1 (you are travelling in Taiwan, took photos with some local people in Tainan and want to mail the photos to them) and Instruction A; Student B reads Scenario 2 (you bought souvenirs in Taiwan and want to send them home to your family) and Instruction B; follow the instruction to fill out the envelopes. B. Use the envelope you filled out to teach each other how to do it properly. Note: unlike addresses written in English, a Chinese address puts the postal code first, followed by larger to smaller units (city, road/street/alley, house number). The book prints the instructions mostly in traditional characters (and gives links to animations at the Taiwan post office website); here they are in simplified characters:

rows: 10645 台北市大安區師大路 9 号
70101 台南市东区大学路一号
10461 台北市中山北路 4 段 1 号
tables.title: The addresses in Activity 2 (the book’s digits are the postal codes and house numbers; the postal code goes first, then larger to smaller units)

examples.text: 国内邮件直式信封书写方式：第一步，把收信人的姓名写在信封的中间，地址写在信封的右边，邮递区号用阿拉伯数字写在信封右上方的红框格内。
examples.translation: guó nèi yóu jiàn zhí shì xìn fēng shū xiě fāng shì dì yī bù bǎ shōu xìn rén de xìng míng xiě zài xìn fēng de zhōng jiān dì zhǐ xiě zài xìn fēng de yòu biān yóu dì qū hào yòng ā lā bó shù zì xiě zài xìn fēng yòu shàng fāng de hóng kuāng gé nèi — Instruction A, how to write a vertical envelope for domestic mail. Step 1: write the addressee’s name in the middle of the envelope and the address on the right side, and the postal code in Arabic numerals in the red boxes at the upper right of the envelope.

examples.text: 第二步，把寄信人地址、姓名写在信封的左下方，邮递区号以阿拉伯数字写在信封左下方红框格内。
examples.translation: dì èr bù bǎ jì xìn rén dì zhǐ xìng míng xiě zài xìn fēng de zuǒ xià fāng yóu dì qū hào yǐ ā lā bó shù zì xiě zài xìn fēng zuǒ xià fāng hóng kuāng gé nèi — Step 2: write the sender’s address and name at the lower left of the envelope, and the postal code in Arabic numerals in the red boxes at the lower left.

examples.text: 第三步，最后把邮票贴在信封左上方。
examples.translation: dì sān bù zuì hòu bǎ yóu piào tiē zài xìn fēng zuǒ shàng fāng — Step 3: finally stick the stamp at the upper left of the envelope.

examples.text: 国外邮件信封书写方式：第一步，把收信人的地址、姓名和邮递区号写在信封中间靠右的地方。
examples.translation: guó wài yóu jiàn xìn fēng shū xiě fāng shì dì yī bù bǎ shōu xìn rén de dì zhǐ xìng míng hé yóu dì qū hào xiě zài xìn fēng zhōng jiān kào yòu de dì fāng — Instruction B, how to write an envelope for international mail. Step 1: write the addressee’s address, name and postal code in the middle, toward the right, of the envelope.

examples.text: 第二步，把寄信人地址、姓名和邮递区号写在信封左上方或信封的后面。
examples.translation: dì èr bù bǎ jì xìn rén dì zhǐ xìng míng hé yóu dì qū hào xiě zài xìn fēng zuǒ shàng fāng huò xìn fēng de hòu miàn — Step 2: write the sender’s address, name and postal code at the upper left or on the back of the envelope.

examples.text: 第三步，最后把邮票贴在信封的右上方。
examples.translation: dì sān bù zuì hòu bǎ yóu piào tiē zài xìn fēng de yòu shàng fāng — Step 3: finally stick the stamp at the upper right of the envelope.

explanations.title: Activity 2C and Activity 3
explanations.body: C. The format of mailing a domestic letter in China is different than in the U.S. Listen to a short passage and write an English summary of it. (Audio, not included.) Activity 3 (Reading, Speaking, Listening and Writing): You are in Taiwan for immersion learning and have learned some facts about the postal services in Taiwan; your teachers would like to know about the postal services in the U.S. A. Form groups of three and list the functions of both the U.S. and the Taiwanese postal service (the book points to the Taiwanese Postal Service website and the U.S. postal service’s Chinese website; links are not included). B. Use the Venn diagram (台湾的邮局 | 美国的邮局, not included) to illustrate the similarities and differences. C. Make a presentation to the class in Chinese describing the American and Taiwanese postal services. D. The class takes notes and votes for the best presentation. lessons.title: 511. Lesson 20 Presentation 3: the post office then and now
lessons.subtitle: 几十年前的邮局 · 电子邮件和微信 · 代理业务 · 国家队 万能手

explanations.title: Getting Started
explanations.body: Pair up and discuss: A. Can you name several traditional services offered by the U.S. post office? B. Do you know any additional services provided by the post office? C. What factors have impacted the post office’s operation in the U.S.? (Four small pictures, not included.)

explanations.title: Presentation 3: 中国邮政的过去和现在
explanations.body: The passage is in three paragraphs; the book also prints it in traditional characters. The percentage and the volume (80%, 400 亿) are written in characters here. The translations are mine.

examples.text: 说起几十年前的中国邮政，四、五十岁的人都会记起那些虽然不大，但是非常繁忙的邮局。那时候，人们每隔几天就要去一趟邮局。买邮票，寄信，寄包裹要去邮局，打长途，发电报，也得去邮局，订报纸、杂志，给爷爷奶奶汇钱，还要去邮局，邮局和人们的日常生活简直是分不开。
examples.translation: shuō qǐ jǐ shí nián qián de zhōng guó yóu zhèng sì wǔ shí suì de rén dōu huì jì qǐ nà xiē suī rán bú dà dàn shì fēi cháng fán máng de yóu jú nà shí hòu rén men měi gé jǐ tiān jiù yào qù yí tàng yóu jú mǎi yóu piào jì xìn jì bāo guǒ yào qù yóu jú dǎ cháng tú fā diàn bào yě děi qù yóu jú dìng bào zhǐ zá zhì gěi yé yé nǎi nǎi huì qián hái yào qù yóu jú yóu jú hé rén men de rì cháng shēng huó jiǎn zhí shì fēn bù kāi — Speaking of the Chinese post of several decades ago, people in their forties and fifties will all remember those post offices that were not big but were very busy. In those days people had to go to the post office every few days. To buy stamps, send letters and send parcels you went to the post office; to make long-distance calls and send telegrams you also had to go to the post office; to subscribe to newspapers and magazines and to remit money to Grandpa and Grandma you still had to go to the post office. The post office and people’s daily life were simply inseparable. (translation mine)

examples.text: 可是，电子邮件的发明，却使邮局一下子减少了百分之八十以上的邮件业务。手机、微信的出现更使邮局失去了几乎所有的电讯业务。另外，快递公司的出现也使邮局的快件业务少了一大半。邮局在人们生活中不那么重要了，去邮局的人也越来越少。
examples.translation: kě shì diàn zi yóu jiàn de fā míng què shǐ yóu jú yí xià zi jiǎn shǎo le bǎi fēn zhī bā shí yǐ shàng de yóu jiàn yè wù shǒu jī wēi xìn de chū xiàn gèng shǐ yóu jú shī qù le jī hū suǒ yǒu de diàn xùn yè wù lìng wài kuài dì gōng sī de chū xiàn yě shǐ yóu jú de kuài jiàn yè wù shǎo le yí dà bàn yóu jú zài rén men shēng huó zhōng bú nà me zhòng yào le qù yóu jú de rén yě yuè lái yuè shǎo — But the invention of e-mail suddenly cut the post office’s mail business by more than 80 percent (the book writes 80%). The appearance of mobile phones and WeChat made the post office lose almost all of its telecommunications business. In addition, the appearance of express companies also cut the post office’s express business by more than half. The post office was no longer so important in people’s lives, and fewer and fewer people went to it. (mine)

examples.text: 为了“活”下去，邮局扩大了自己的业务，开始了各种代理业务。代理保险，代售手机卡，代发工资，代收水电费，再次把人们的生活和邮局联系在一起，邮局又慢慢忙起来。邮局还改进了自己的快递业务，使年快递量达到四百亿件。现在，邮局不但活了下来，而且发展得越来越好，被人们叫做快递中的“国家队”，生活中的“万能手”。
examples.translation: wèi le huó xià qù yóu jú kuò dà le zì jǐ de yè wù kāi shǐ le gè zhǒng dài lǐ yè wù dài lǐ bǎo xiǎn dài shòu shǒu jī kǎ dài fā gōng zī dài shōu shuǐ diàn fèi zài cì bǎ rén men de shēng huó hé yóu jú lián xì zài yì qǐ yóu jú yòu màn màn máng qǐ lái yóu jú hái gǎi jìn le zì jǐ de kuài dì yè wù shǐ nián kuài dì liàng dá dào sì bǎi yì jiàn xiàn zài yóu jú bú dàn huó le xià lái ér qiě fā zhǎn de yuè lái yuè hǎo bèi rén men jiào zuò kuài dì zhōng de guó jiā duì shēng huó zhōng de wàn néng shǒu — In order to “live” on, the post office expanded its business and started all kinds of agency business. Acting as an insurance agent, selling SIM cards, paying wages on behalf of companies and collecting water and electricity bills tied people’s lives and the post office together again, and the post office gradually became busy again. It also improved its express business so that the yearly express volume reached 40 billion items (the book writes 400 亿). Now the post office has not only survived but is developing better and better, and people call it the “national team” of express delivery and the “all-rounder” of daily life. (mine)

explanations.body: A. In the sentences below, highlight the subject, verb/verb phrase and object in each sentence, then translate each sentence. B. Pair up and check your answers. The book prints the five sentences and leaves blanks; my analysis and translations:

examples.text: 说起几十年前的中国邮政，四、五十岁的人都会记起那些虽然不大，但是非常繁忙的邮局。
examples.translation: shuō qǐ jǐ shí nián qián de zhōng guó yóu zhèng sì wǔ shí suì de rén dōu huì jì qǐ nà xiē suī rán bú dà dàn shì fēi cháng fán máng de yóu jú — 1. Subject: 四、五十岁的人; verb phrase: 会记起; object: 那些…邮局. Speaking of the Chinese post of several decades ago, people in their forties and fifties will all remember those post offices that were not big but were very busy. (analysis and translation mine)

examples.text: 电子邮件的发明，使邮局一下子减少了百分之八十以上的邮件业务。

Subject: 电子邮件的发明; verb: 使 (the object 邮局 is also the subject of 减少了); object: 业务 (减少了…业务). The invention of e-mail suddenly cut the post office’s mail business by more than 80 percent. (mine)

Subject: 邮局; verb: 改进了; object: 自己的快递业务; 使… makes the yearly express volume reach 40 billion items. The post office also improved its own express business, so that the yearly express volume reached 40 billion items. (mine)

Subject: the four agency services; 把 phrase: 把人们的生活和邮局; verb: 联系在一起. Acting as insurance agent, selling SIM cards, paying wages for others and collecting water and electricity bills tied people’s lives and the post office together again. (mine)

Subject: 邮局; verbs: 活了下来, 发展, 被…叫做; object (of the passive): 国家队, 万能手. explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading)
explanations.body: Select the word that does not belong in the group: 1. 增加 | 发展 | 扩大 | 失去. 2. 但是 | 而且 | 不过 | 却. 3. 另外 | 加上 | 不过 | 还有. 4. 发明 | 产生 | 出现 | 万能. 5. 失去 | 增加 | 减少 | 降低. My answers (the book prints no key): 1. 失去 (the others mean grow, expand or increase); 2. 而且 (the others all mean “but”); 3. 不过 (the others add information); 4. 万能 (the others mean something comes into being); 5. 增加 (the others mean to lose or decrease).

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Compare the following passage (about Chunghwa Post in Taiwan, from zh.wikipedia.org) with the Presentation and write down any similarities or differences in the table. B. Can you guess the meaning of the new, underlined words 貸款, 集郵, 分行, 掙錢? My guesses: 贷款 a loan, 集邮 stamp collecting, 分行 a branch (of a bank), 挣钱 to earn money. The book prints the passage in traditional characters (simplified here):

rows: 邮局都有快递和包裹业务；电子通信和快递公司的出现都使邮政业务减少
中华邮政分为邮务和银行两大业务，银行和保险是最挣钱的业务，存款是台湾第一；大陆的邮局靠代理业务和改进快递“活”了下来，年快递量达到四百亿件

examples.text: 中华邮政的业务分为邮务和银行两大业务。邮政业务包括邮件寄送与快递，银行业务包括存款、提款、汇款，各种保险、房屋贷款。其他服务还包括集邮、代售商品等。中华邮政在全国各地共有邮局一千三百二十二处，如果把邮局当作是一般银行的分行，邮局是营业点最多的银行。
examples.translation: zhōng huá yóu zhèng de yè wù fēn wéi yóu wù hé yín háng liǎng dà yè wù yóu zhèng yè wù bāo kuò yóu jiàn jì sòng yǔ kuài dì yín háng yè wù bāo kuò cún kuǎn tí kuǎn huì kuǎn gè zhǒng bǎo xiǎn fáng wū dài kuǎn qí tā fú wù hái bāo kuò jí yóu dài shòu shāng pǐn děng zhōng huá yóu zhèng zài quán guó gè dì gòng yǒu yóu jú yì qiān sān bǎi èr shí èr chù rú guǒ bǎ yóu jú dàng zuò shì yì bān yín háng de fēn háng yóu jú shì yíng yè diǎn zuì duō de yín háng — Chunghwa Post’s business is divided into two big businesses, postal and banking. Postal business includes mail delivery and express, banking business includes deposits, withdrawals, remittances, all kinds of insurance and housing loans. Other services also include stamp collecting and selling goods as an agent. Chunghwa Post has 1,322 post offices across the country (the book writes 1322); if you regard post offices as branches of an ordinary bank, the post office is the bank with the most business locations. (the book prints it in traditional characters; translation mine)

examples.text: 近几年来，虽然电话、网际网络等电子通信方式的发达，以及其它快递公司的加入，使得中华邮政的邮务业务大量减少，但因邮局的快递与包裹服务等定价还是比其它快递公司便宜，因此，中华邮政的快递和包裹业务还是发展得相当快。另外，中华邮政的银行业务以及保险业务也已经远远超过邮局的邮政业务，成为邮局最挣钱的业务。邮局的存款金额更是全台湾银行中的第一位。
examples.translation: jìn jǐ nián lái suī rán diàn huà wǎng jì wǎng luò děng diàn zi tōng xìn fāng shì de fā dá yǐ jí qí tā kuài dì gōng sī de jiā rù shǐ de zhōng huá yóu zhèng de yóu wù yè wù dà liàng jiǎn shǎo dàn yīn yóu jú de kuài dì yǔ bāo guǒ fú wù děng dìng jià hái shì bǐ qí tā kuài dì gōng sī pián yi yīn cǐ zhōng huá yóu zhèng de kuài dì hé bāo guǒ yè wù hái shì fā zhǎn de xiāng dāng kuài lìng wài zhōng huá yóu zhèng de yín háng yè wù yǐ jí bǎo xiǎn yè wù yě yǐ jīng yuǎn yuǎn chāo guò yóu jú de yóu zhèng yè wù chéng wéi yóu jú zuì zhèng qián de yè wù yóu jú de cún kuǎn jīn é gèng shì quán tái wān yín háng zhōng de dì yī wèi — In recent years, although electronic means of communication such as the telephone and the internet have developed, and other express companies have joined in, so that Chunghwa Post’s postal business has greatly decreased, the prices of the post office’s express and parcel services are still cheaper than those of the other express companies, so Chunghwa Post’s express and parcel business is still developing quite fast. In addition, Chunghwa Post’s banking and insurance businesses have already far surpassed its postal business and become the post office’s most profitable business. The post office’s deposit total is even number one among all banks in Taiwan. (the book prints it mostly in traditional characters; translation mine)

lessons.title: 513. Lesson 20 Presentation 3 grammar: the causative verb 使 (and 让)
lessons.subtitle: 电子邮件的出现使邮局…减少了 · 使 比 让 正式 · 让 = 命令 允许 请求

explanations.title: The Causative Verb 使
explanations.body: The causative verb 使 is used to express the idea that A (the cause or condition) makes B change to a specific state or take an action (i.e., a result or effect): A 使 B (adjective or verb phrase). Although 使 and 让 can be translated as “make/cause” in English and are sometimes used interchangeably, they differ in their usage due to their meaning. 1. 使 tends to be used more in formal/written situations while 让 is used in a more colloquial style. 2. When 使 is used in a sentence, the result can be a state; when 让 is used the result can be either a state or an action. 3. 让 can also mean giving permission, making a request, or giving orders; in this situation only 让 is allowed.

tables.title: The causative verb 使: A 使 B (adj. or verb phrase)

examples.text: 电子邮件的出现使邮局的邮政业务减少了一大半。
examples.translation: diàn zi yóu jiàn de chū xiàn shǐ yóu jú de yóu zhèng yè wù jiǎn shǎo le yí dà bàn — (formal) The appearance of e-mail cut the post office’s postal business by more than half.

examples.text: 电子邮件的出现让邮局的邮政业务减少了一大半。
examples.translation: diàn zi yóu jiàn de chū xiàn ràng yóu jú de yóu zhèng yè wù jiǎn shǎo le yí dà bàn — (less formal) The same sentence with 让.

examples.text: 电子邮件的出现使邮局的邮政业务减少了一大半。
examples.translation: diàn zi yóu jiàn de chū xiàn shǐ yóu jú de yóu zhèng yè wù jiǎn shǎo le yí dà bàn — (state) The result of 使 is a state: the postal business decreased.

examples.text: 邮政业务的减少让邮局开始增加许多代理业务。
examples.translation: yóu zhèng yè wù de jiǎn shǎo ràng yóu jú kāi shǐ zēng jiā xǔ duō dài lǐ yè wù — (action) The decrease of the postal business made the post office begin adding many agency businesses (an action, so 让).

examples.text: 老师让同学明天带作业本来。
examples.translation: lǎo shī ràng tóng xué míng tiān dài zuò yè běn lái — (give orders) The teacher tells the students to bring their workbooks tomorrow. (the book prints 作业书, which I read as 作业本)

examples.text: 妈妈让我做完作业看三十分钟电视。
examples.translation: mā mā ràng wǒ zuò wán zuò yè kàn sān shí fēn zhōng diàn shì — (give permission) Mom lets me watch thirty minutes of TV after I finish my homework. (the book writes 30)

examples.text: 他让我午休的时候帮他买一杯咖啡。
examples.translation: tā ràng wǒ wǔ xiū de shí hòu bāng tā mǎi yì bēi kā fēi — (make a request) He asked me to buy him a cup of coffee at the lunch break.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Pair up. Each partner uses the topics in one of the columns to create a sentence using 使; the partner translates the sentence. Student B’s topics: 参军 (参加陆军/空军/海军), 上语法课/听力课/说话课, 锻炼身体, 网路的发明. My sentences:

examples.translation: qù bù tóng dì fāng lǚ xíng shǐ wǒ rèn shí le hěn duō xīn péng yǒu — Traveling to different places made me meet many new friends. (A, mine)

examples.text: 玩电子游戏使我的眼睛很累。
examples.translation: wán diàn zǐ yóu xì shǐ wǒ de yǎn jīng hěn lèi — Playing video games makes my eyes very tired. (A, mine)

examples.text: 手机的出现使人们的生活方便多了。
examples.translation: shǒu jī de chū xiàn shǐ rén men de shēng huó fāng biàn duō le — The appearance of mobile phones made people’s lives much more convenient. (A, mine)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading)
explanations.body: A. Complete the sentences with either 让 or 使, or both, and provide your rationale. B. Check your answers with your partner. The book prints the five sentences with blanks and no key; my answers:

(key mine)

lessons.title: 514. Lesson 20 Presentation 3 grammar: the passive 被 in a neutral context
lessons.subtitle: 被叫做 被称为 被选为 被分成 · 被翻译成 被派往 被录取 · 句子重组

explanations.title: The Passive Voice of 被 in a Neutral Context
explanations.body: 被 is used to express the passive voice in a sentence. In a passive-voice sentence the object of an action becomes the subject of the sentence, and the doer of the action, which would have been the subject of the normal (active-voice) sentence, becomes secondary and may or may not be mentioned: A (recipient) 被 (B, doer) verb (+ complement). The 被 structure is often used to express an adverse or unfortunate situation, or to express the disposition of the object in the same way the 把 construction does; in this lesson we focus on 被 in a neutral context. There it often accompanies 为 or 做, as in 被称为, 被选为, 被叫做. Other neutral contexts are shown in examples 5 to 7. The book’s adverse examples first:

tables.title: The passive voice with 被: A 被 B + verb (+ complement)

examples.text: 他被人打了。
examples.translation: tā bèi rén dǎ le — He was hit by someone. (the book’s adverse example)

examples.text: 我们公司的申请表都被找工作的人拿完了。
examples.translation: wǒ men gōng sī de shēn qǐng biǎo dōu bèi zhǎo gōng zuò de rén ná wán le — All of our company’s application forms were taken by job seekers. (the book’s adverse example)

examples.text: 邮局被人们叫做快递中的“国家队”，生活中的“万能手”。
examples.translation: yóu jú bèi rén men jiào zuò kuài dì zhōng de guó jiā duì shēng huó zhōng de wàn néng shǒu — 1. The post office is called by people the “national team” of express delivery and the “all-rounder” of daily life.

examples.text: 他被选为我们的班长。
examples.translation: tā bèi xuǎn wèi wǒ men de bān zhǎng — 2. He was elected our class monitor.

examples.text: 我们被分成两个小组。
examples.translation: wǒ men bèi fēn chéng liǎng gè xiǎo zǔ — 3. We were divided into two groups.

examples.text: 重庆又被叫做、称为中国的雾都。
examples.translation: chóng qìng yòu bèi jiào zuò chēng wéi zhōng guó de wù dōu — 4. Chongqing is also called China’s “city of fog” (the book writes 叫做/称为 with a slash).

examples.text: 这本书很受欢迎，被翻译成许多国的语言。
examples.translation: zhè běn shū hěn shòu huān yíng bèi fān yì chéng xǔ duō guó de yǔ yán — 5. This book is very popular and has been translated into the languages of many countries.

examples.text: 因为她的外语能力好，她常被派往许多城市出差。
examples.translation: yīn wèi tā de wài yǔ néng lì hǎo tā cháng bèi pài wǎng xǔ duō chéng shì chū chāi — 6. Because her foreign-language ability is good, she is often sent to many cities on business trips.

examples.text: 他高考考得很不错，所以被北京大学录取了。
examples.translation: tā gāo kǎo kǎo de hěn bú cuò suǒ yǐ bèi běi jīng dà xué lù qǔ le — 7. He did quite well in the college entrance exam, so he was admitted to Peking University.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: Reorder the following phrases into a grammatically correct and logical sentence and then translate them. 1. 叫做 | 纽约 | 被 大苹果 | 许多人. 2. 当地人 称为 芝加哥 被 凤城. 3. 被 他 当 这所学校 请去 语文老师. 4. 我妈妈 包 家事 了 所有的 都 被. 5. 妈妈 叫起来 每天早上 6 点 他 就 被 学习 了. 6. 包裹 退回来 邮局 被 了. The book leaves the translation lines blank; my sentences and translations:

examples.text: 纽约被许多人叫做大苹果。
examples.translation: niǔ yuē bèi xǔ duō rén jiào zuò dà píng guǒ — 1. New York is called the Big Apple by many people. (my order)

examples.text: 芝加哥被当地人称为风城。
examples.translation: zhī jiā gē bèi dāng dì rén chēng wéi fēng chéng — 2. Chicago is called the “Windy City” by the locals. (mine; the book prints 凤城, which I read as 风城)

examples.text: 他被这所学校请去当语文老师。
examples.translation: tā bèi zhè suǒ xué xiào qǐng qù dāng yǔ wén lǎo shī — 3. He was invited by this school to be a Chinese teacher. (mine)

examples.text: 所有的家事都被我妈妈包了。
examples.translation: suǒ yǒu de jiā shì dōu bèi wǒ mā mā bāo le — 4. All the housework has been taken over by my mother. (mine)

examples.text: 每天早上六点他就被妈妈叫起来学习了。
examples.translation: měi tiān zǎo shàng liù diǎn tā jiù bèi mā mā jiào qǐ lái xué xí le — 5. Every morning at six he is woken up by his mother to study. (mine; the book writes 6)

examples.text: 包裹被邮局退回来了。
examples.translation: bāo guǒ bèi yóu jú tuì huí lái le — 6. The parcel was returned by the post office. (mine)

exercises.prompt: In a 被 sentence, what becomes the subject?
exercises.explanation: The object of the action becomes the subject.

exercises.prompt: Where does the doer go in 被 sentences?
options: After 被, before the verb (and it may be omitted)

exercises.prompt: Which words often go with 被 in a neutral context?
options: 为 and 做 (被称为, 被叫做)
exercises.explanation: 被称为, 被选为, 被叫做.

options: 两个小组我们被分了成。
许多人纽约被叫做大苹果。
纽约被许多人叫做大苹果。
被纽约许多人叫做大苹果。
纽约叫做许多人被大苹果。
exercises.explanation: New York is called the Big Apple by many people.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is an adverse (unfortunate) 被 example from the book?
options: 重庆又被叫做中国的雾都。

exercises.prompt: What does 他被北京大学录取了 mean?
options: He was admitted to Peking University

lessons.title: 515. Lesson 20 Presentation 3 grammar: 另外, 还有 and 而且
lessons.subtitle: 另外 = by the way · 还有 = in addition to · 而且 = furthermore

explanations.title: The Usage of 另外
explanations.body: As a conjunction, 另外 can link two sentences, indicating “in addition to” or “besides.” It is often followed by 还 or 也: Sentence, 另外, Sentence. 另外, 而且 and 还有 share similar meanings and are often used interchangeably. However, compared to 而且 and 还有, 另外 has a softer tone and a meaning similar to the English “by the way,” so it is usually followed by a less important point that the speaker wants to mention. 还有 is stronger in tone, similar to “in addition to” and more colloquial, while 而且 also has a stronger tone, tends to be more formal and expresses “furthermore.”

tables.title: 另外, 还有 and 而且 (the book’s table)

examples.text: 特快专递最快，另外，价钱也不贵。
examples.translation: tè kuài zhuān dì zuì kuài lìng wài jià qián yě bú guì — Express is fastest. By the way, the price isn’t high either. (pattern: sentence, 另外, sentence; mine)

examples.text: 他会说中文，另外，他还会说日文。
examples.translation: tā huì shuō zhōng wén lìng wài tā hái huì shuō rì wén — He can speak Chinese; in addition he can also speak Japanese. (另外 followed by 还; mine)

examples.text: 邮局可以寄信，另外，也可以代收水电费。
examples.translation: yóu jú kě yǐ jì xìn lìng wài yě kě yǐ dài shōu shuǐ diàn fèi — The post office can send letters, and in addition can collect utility bills. (另外 followed by 也; mine)

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Writing)
explanations.body: A. Think of your favorite hobby and write several reasons why you enjoy it (我喜欢(hobby)。原因：1. 2. 3.). B. Use the key elements from your list to write a short paragraph about your hobby using 另外, 而且 or 还有. My sample paragraph:

examples.text: 我喜欢跑步。原因有三个：第一，跑步对身体好。第二，跑步不用花很多钱，也不用找人一起去。另外，跑步以后我觉得很轻松，晚上睡得也好。而且在公园里跑步还可以认识很多新朋友。还有，每天早上跑步使我一天都很有精神。
examples.translation: wǒ xǐ huān pǎo bù yuán yīn yǒu sān gè dì yī pǎo bù duì shēn tǐ hǎo dì èr pǎo bù bú yòng huā hěn duō qián yě bú yòng zhǎo rén yì qǐ qù lìng wài pǎo bù yǐ hòu wǒ jué de hěn qīng sōng wǎn shàng shuì de yě hǎo ér qiě zài gōng yuán lǐ pǎo bù hái kě yǐ rèn shí hěn duō xīn péng yǒu hái yǒu měi tiān zǎo shàng pǎo bù shǐ wǒ yì tiān dōu hěn yǒu jīng shén — I like running. There are three reasons: first, running is good for the body. Second, running doesn’t cost much, and you don’t need to find someone to go with. In addition, after running I feel relaxed and I sleep well at night. Moreover, running in the park I can meet many new friends. Also, running every morning keeps me energetic all day. (my sample paragraph; the book leaves the space for your own hobby, reasons 1 to 3 and a short paragraph using 另外, 而且 or 还有)

exercises.prompt: Which of 另外, 还有, 而且 has the softest tone?

options: A less important point the speaker wants to mention

exercises.prompt: What often follows 另外 in the same clause?

options: 另外 at the end of a sentence

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 另外 well?
options: 特快专递最快另外另外。
特快专递另外最快价钱。
特快专递最快，另外，价钱也不贵。

lessons.title: 516. Lesson 20 Presentation 3 grammar: 所有的 and 都
lessons.subtitle: 所有的 + noun · 所有的和都一起用 · 什么都没有 · 全都

explanations.title: The Use of 所有的
explanations.body: 所有的 serves as an adjective and is usually followed by a noun. It means “all,” or “all of …”: 所有的 + noun. 所有的 vs 都: 所有的 is an adjective, generally followed by a noun, while 都 is an adverb, usually placed after a subject and followed by a verb. 所有的 and 都 often appear together in one sentence to express the meaning “all.”

examples.text: 手机、微信的出现使邮局失去了所有的电讯业务。
examples.translation: shǒu jī wēi xìn de chū xiàn shǐ yóu jú shī qù le suǒ yǒu de diàn xùn yè wù — 1. The appearance of mobile phones and WeChat made the post office lose all of its telecommunications business.

examples.text: 我们班所有的同学都是军人。
examples.translation: wǒ men bān suǒ yǒu de tóng xué dōu shì jūn rén — 2. All the students in our class are servicemen.

examples.text: 我把所有的时间都花在学习中文上。
examples.translation: wǒ bǎ suǒ yǒu de shí jiān dōu huā zài xué xí zhōng wén shàng — 3. I spend all my time on studying Chinese.

examples.text: 他把他所有的钱都拿去买房子了。
examples.translation: tā bǎ tā suǒ yǒu de qián dōu ná qù mǎi fáng zi le — 4. He took all his money and bought a house.

examples.text: 梅西百货大楼所有的商品都打八折。
examples.translation: méi xī bǎi huò dà lóu suǒ yǒu de shāng pǐn dōu dǎ bā zhé — 1. All the goods in Macy’s department store are 20 percent off. (所有的 and 都 together)

examples.text: 梅西百货大楼商品都打八折。
examples.translation: méi xī bǎi huò dà lóu shāng pǐn dōu dǎ bā zhé — 2. The goods in Macy’s department store are all 20 percent off. (都 only)

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Reading)
explanations.body: Choose the correct sentence and check your answer with a classmate. Set 1: 1. 大家都出去！ 2. 什么都出去！ 3. 所有的都出去。 Set 2: 1. 她的皮包里什么都没有。 2. 她的皮包里都没有。 3. 她的皮包里所有的都没。 Set 3: 1. 音乐厅里所有的人都站了起来。 2. 音乐厅里的人都站了起来。 3. 音乐厅里的人什么都站了起来。 The book prints no key; my choices are Set 1: 1; Set 2: 1; Set 3: 1 and 2 (2 is also correct but without the stress of 所有的), and 3 is wrong:

examples.text: 大家都出去！

lessons.title: 517. Lesson 20 Presentation 3 skill integration: your mailing habits, the U.S. and Taiwan post offices

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Listening, Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: A. Take a few minutes to study the following questions. Then use them to acquire information from your classmates and fill in the table. B. The class shares their findings in Chinese. The eight questions (the table is not included; the translations are mine):

examples.text: 你上次寄包裹是什么时候？你去哪儿寄？怎么寄？
examples.translation: nǐ shàng cì jì bāo guǒ shì shén me shí hòu nǐ qù nǎr jì zěn me jì — 1. When was the last time you mailed a parcel? Where did you go to mail it? How?

examples.text: 你平常寄信、寄贺卡吗？你什么时候会寄？
examples.translation: nǐ píng cháng jì xìn jì hè kǎ ma nǐ shén me shí hòu huì jì — 2. Do you usually mail letters or greeting cards? When do you mail them?

examples.text: 如果你不寄信，你常用什么方式和家人朋友联系？
examples.translation: rú guǒ nǐ bú jì xìn nǐ cháng yòng shén me fāng shì hé jiā rén péng yǒu lián xì — 3. If you don’t mail letters, what way do you often use to keep in touch with family and friends?

examples.text: 你用过邮局或银行的什么代理业务？
examples.translation: nǐ yòng guò yóu jú huò yín háng de shén me dài lǐ yè wù — 4. What agency services of the post office or a bank have you used?

examples.text: 你最常用美国邮局的哪个服务？为什么？
examples.translation: nǐ zuì cháng yòng měi guó yóu jú de nǎ ge fú wù wèi shén me — 5. Which U.S. Postal Service service do you use most often? Why?

examples.text: 你租过美国邮局的信箱或用他们办过护照吗？你觉得怎么样？
examples.translation: nǐ zū guò měi guó yóu jú de xìn xiāng huò yòng tā men bàn guò hù zhào ma nǐ jué de zěn me yàng — 6. Have you rented a P.O. box at a U.S. post office or applied for a passport through them? What did you think?

examples.text: 你网购以后退过东西吗？你怎么把东西寄回去？
examples.translation: nǐ wǎng gòu yǐ hòu tuì guò dōng xī ma nǐ zěn me bǎ dōng xī jì huí qù — 7. Have you returned something after buying online? How did you send it back?

examples.text: 网路的发明使你增加了什么？减少了什么？失去了什么？
examples.translation: wǎng lù de fā míng shǐ nǐ zēng jiā le shén me jiǎn shǎo le shén me shī qù le shén me — 8. What has the invention of the internet added for you? What has it reduced? What has it made you lose?

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading, Speaking and Writing)
explanations.body: A. Read the passage from a Chinese immigrant’s blog, take notes on the differences between the postal service in the U.S. and Taiwan, and fill in the table. B. Pair up and share your answers in Chinese with your partner. The passage, then my notes:

rows: 一般只办邮局的普通业务：寄信、寄包裹、买邮票、买信封
除了邮局业务以外，还有银行和许多其它的代理业务
留交邮件（出差或旅行时让邮局保留信件，回家后再送还）；代办护照（填好申请表，准备好照片和申请费，预约一个时间）
tables.title: Activity 3A: the post office in the U.S. and in Taiwan (the book leaves the table blank; this is my filling)

examples.text: 我来美国以后才知道美国的邮局和台湾的邮局不太一样。第一，他们的颜色不同。美国邮局的颜色是蓝色，台湾的是绿色。第二，他们的服务也有些不一样。美国的邮局一般只办邮局的普通业务，不像台湾的邮局还有银行和许多其它的代理业务。所以美国人去邮局多半是为了寄信、寄包裹、买邮票、买信封什么的。另外，美国邮局还有一个特别的服务，那就是留交邮件的服务。要是你常出差或旅行，你可以在旅行或出差前，到邮局的网站填一张表，告诉邮局你什么时候不在家，这样邮局可以帮你保留信件。等你回到家，他们还会把信都送还给你。当然，你也可以亲自去邮局领取。最后，美国邮局还有一个台湾邮局没有的服务，那就是美国邮局可以代办护照。只要你先填好护照申请表，准备好照片和申请费，你就可以跟邮局预约一个时间到邮局去申请护照，非常方便。
examples.translation: wǒ lái měi guó yǐ hòu cái zhī dào měi guó de yóu jú hé tái wān de yóu jú bú tài yí yàng dì yī tā men de yán sè bù tóng měi guó yóu jú de yán sè shì lán sè tái wān de shì lǜ sè dì èr tā men de fú wù yě yǒu xiē bù yí yàng měi guó de yóu jú yì bān zhǐ bàn yóu jú de pǔ tōng yè wù bú xiàng tái wān de yóu jú hái yǒu yín háng hé xǔ duō qí tā de dài lǐ yè wù suǒ yǐ měi guó rén qù yóu jú duō bàn shì wèi le jì xìn jì bāo guǒ mǎi yóu piào mǎi xìn fēng shén me de lìng wài měi guó yóu jú hái yǒu yí gè tè bié de fú wù nà jiù shì liú jiāo yóu jiàn de fú wù yào shì nǐ cháng chū chāi huò lǚ xíng nǐ kě yǐ zài lǚ xíng huò chū chāi qián dào yóu jú de wǎng zhàn tián yì zhāng biǎo gào sù yóu jú nǐ shén me shí hòu bú zài jiā zhè yàng yóu jú kě yǐ bāng nǐ bǎo liú xìn jiàn děng nǐ huí dào jiā tā men hái huì bǎ xìn dōu sòng huán gěi nǐ dāng rán nǐ yě kě yǐ qīn zì qù yóu jú lǐng qǔ zuì hòu měi guó yóu jú hái yǒu yí gè tái wān yóu jú méi yǒu de fú wù nà jiù shì měi guó yóu jú kě yǐ dài bàn hù zhào zhǐ yào nǐ xiān tián hǎo hù zhào shēn qǐng biǎo zhǔn bèi hǎo zhào piān hé shēn qǐng fèi nǐ jiù kě yǐ gēn yóu jú yù yuē yí gè shí jiān dào yóu jú qù shēn qǐng hù zhào fēi cháng fāng biàn — After I came to America I learned that American post offices and Taiwanese post offices are not quite the same. First, their colors are different: the American post office is blue, Taiwan’s is green. Second, their services are also somewhat different. American post offices generally handle only ordinary post-office business, not like Taiwan’s post office, which also has banking and many other agency services. So Americans mostly go to the post office to send letters, send parcels, buy stamps, buy envelopes and so on. In addition, the American post office has a special service, which is the hold-mail service. If you often go on business trips or travel, before you travel you can fill in a form on the post office’s website to tell the post office when you will not be at home, and then the post office can hold your mail for you. When you get home they will also send all the mail back to you. Of course you can also go to the post office in person and pick it up. Last, the American post office has a service the Taiwanese post office does not have: it can handle passports for you. As long as you first fill in the passport application form and prepare the photo and the application fee, you can make an appointment with the post office for a time to go there and apply for a passport, which is very convenient. (the book prints it in a mix of traditional and simplified characters; translation mine)

lessons.title: 518. Lesson 20 Presentation 3 using Chinese in context: drop boxes, i邮箱 and mailing services in Taiwan
lessons.subtitle: 邮筒 红色和绿色 · 夜间的服务 · 爱邮箱 · 平信 限时邮件 挂号邮件

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading and Speaking)
explanations.body: New vocabulary: 邮筒 (yóutǒng; post office drop box). Sometimes this can also be called 邮箱 (yóuxiāng), but 邮箱 can also refer to the P.O. box or a mailbox in front of a house. A. Read the passage and answer: 1. Who is the intended audience? 2. What message does the passage try to convey? 3. What solutions are provided? List two. 4. Why are different colors mentioned? B. Pair up and, in Chinese, check your answers. My answers (the book prints none): 1. People who want to mail something but cannot go during working hours. 2. You don’t have to rush to the post office in working hours; you can mail things after work. 3. Drop boxes outside every post office; night service until nine; Saturday half-day. 4. The green box is for ordinary mail (left side for the same city, right side for other cities); the red box is for express mail and mail going abroad. The passage:

examples.text: 你知道吗？到邮局寄信、寄包裹，不用赶在上班时间去。下班以后，还是可以寄东西。为了让老百姓的生活更方便，每个邮局外面都设有邮筒。台湾的邮筒分为红色和绿色的。寄一般的邮件得把信放进绿色的邮筒。绿色的邮筒分为左右两边。一边是寄到本市的信件，另一边是寄到别的县市的信件。如果你的信是快件或是要寄到国外的，那你就得把信放进红色的邮筒。不管你放的是哪个邮筒，寄之前，别忘了填好寄件人和收件人的姓名和地址。当然，最重要的是要贴上足够的邮票。这样邮局才不会把你的信退回来。如果你寄的是包裹，邮局外的邮筒放不进去，这也不要紧。虽然邮局通常营业到下午五点，但是有些邮局提供夜间的服务，最晚开到晚上九点。你只要上邮局的网站查一下就能找到这些信息。另外，多半的邮局星期六还上半天班，这下子，你就不用担心找不到时间去邮局了。
examples.translation: nǐ zhī dào ma dào yóu jú jì xìn jì bāo guǒ bú yòng gǎn zài shàng bān shí jiān qù xià bān yǐ hòu hái shì kě yǐ jì dōng xī wèi le ràng lǎo bǎi xìng de shēng huó gèng fāng biàn měi gè yóu jú wài miàn dōu shè yǒu yóu tǒng tái wān de yóu tǒng fēn wéi hóng sè hé lǜ sè de jì yì bān de yóu jiàn děi bǎ xìn fàng jìn lǜ sè de yóu tǒng lǜ sè de yóu tǒng fēn wéi zuǒ yòu liǎng biān yì biān shì jì dào běn shì de xìn jiàn lìng yì biān shì jì dào bié de xiàn shì de xìn jiàn rú guǒ nǐ de xìn shì kuài jiàn huò shì yào jì dào guó wài de nà nǐ jiù děi bǎ xìn fàng jìn hóng sè de yóu tǒng bù guǎn nǐ fàng de shì nǎ ge yóu tǒng jì zhī qián bié wàng le tián hǎo jì jiàn rén hé shōu jiàn rén de xìng míng hé dì zhǐ dāng rán zuì zhòng yào de shì yào tiē shàng zú gòu de yóu piào zhè yàng yóu jú cái bú huì bǎ nǐ de xìn tuì huí lái rú guǒ nǐ jì de shì bāo guǒ yóu jú wài de yóu tǒng fàng bú jìn qù zhè yě bú yào jǐn suī rán yóu jú tōng cháng yíng yè dào xià wǔ wǔ diǎn dàn shì yǒu xiē yóu jú tí gōng yè jiān de fú wù zuì wǎn kāi dào wǎn shàng jiǔ diǎn nǐ zhǐ yào shàng yóu jú de wǎng zhàn chá yí xià jiù néng zhǎo dào zhè xiē xìn xī lìng wài duō bàn de yóu jú xīng qī liù hái shàng bàn tiān bān zhè xià zi nǐ jiù bú yòng dān xīn zhǎo bú dào shí jiān qù yóu jú le — Did you know? To mail letters or parcels at the post office you don’t have to rush there during working hours. After work you can still mail things. To make the people’s lives more convenient every post office has drop boxes outside. Taiwan’s drop boxes are divided into red and green ones. To send ordinary mail you must put the letter into the green box. The green box is divided into a left and a right side: one side is for letters to the same city, the other for letters to other counties and cities. If your letter is express mail or is going abroad, then you must put it into the red box. Whichever box you use, before mailing don’t forget to fill in the names and addresses of the sender and the recipient. Of course the most important thing is to put on enough stamps; only then will the post office not send your letter back. If you are mailing a parcel and the box outside the post office is too small for it, that’s also fine. Although post offices are usually open until five in the afternoon (the book writes 5 点), some offer night service and stay open until nine at night at the latest (9 点). You only need to check the post office’s website to find this information. In addition, most post offices work half a day on Saturday, so you don’t need to worry about not finding time to go to the post office. (the book has a full stop after “国外的”, which I changed to a comma; translation mine)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading, Listening and Writing)
explanations.body: In order to compete with the other express services, the post office in Taiwan has offered the i 邮箱 service. A. Read the short introduction below about this service and summarize the service it provides. My summary: it is a self-service pick-up and mailing point at post offices and stations, open all year without a break, where you can send letters and parcels, return goods, and have parcels (including online purchases) delivered to it and collect them at the specified time. B. Now use the link (a YouTuber’s video, 1:52–3:49, or a second video) to watch a video about using this service and, in Chinese, write instructions with bullet points for other internet users; post them on Linoit. (Videos and Linoit are not included.) The introduction:

examples.text: 爱邮箱是一种新型的取、寄邮件体验，提供全年无休、自助领取、交寄包裹及退货的服务。您可上网在各地的邮局或车站找到爱邮箱。你不仅可以在爱邮箱寄信、寄包裹，也可用爱邮箱的地址，让收件人直接到爱邮箱领包裹，或是你也可以在网路购物后，请网购公司把你的商品直接寄送到爱邮箱，你再按领件时间到特定的爱邮箱取件就可以了。

lessons.title: 520. Lesson 20 Area Studies: Postal Service in China
lessons.subtitle: 1998年的改革 · 八万二千多个邮局 · E-post · EMS · 二十一世纪的邮政

explanations.title: Postal Service in China (1)
explanations.body: In 1998 China reformed its postal and telecommunications systems and established an independent postal service. The new postal service conforms to the global trend of postal service functions, and has become one of the most important carriers of information, commodities, and financial instruments in China. China Post has accelerated the development of postal services, improved service quality and made postal service more available all over the country. According to statistics from the State Post Bureau, the number of post offices is more than 82,000, with almost 60,000 located in rural areas. This greatly helps the country’s postal service.

explanations.title: Postal Service in China (2)
explanations.body: Instead of traditional businesses such as post-delivery, philately, magazine and newspaper subscription services, China Post, the sole agency in charge of China’s nationwide post services, is relying more and more on postal savings deposits boxes for profit, and is now focusing on the development of E-post (electronic postal service), which includes online remittance, online shopping, online stamp collecting, online newspaper subscription and door-to-door parcel delivery. Post offices, with their eye-catching green emblems, are usually found on main streets, at railway stations, at airports and scenic spots. They are open daily from 09:00–17:00. Domestic mail is very fast and the cost is low, normally 0.8 yuan for local delivery, 1.2 yuan for inter-city mail, 2.50 yuan for Hong Kong and 5.50 yuan for foreign countries.

explanations.title: Postal Service in China (3)
explanations.body: China’s postal service also offers Express Mail Service (EMS). After China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, fierce market competition emerged, with the arrival of many foreign companies. Several international express mail services, such as DHL, UPS, TNT and FedEx, have offices in major Chinese cities. China Post has established direct postal service policies with 220 countries and regions worldwide. China’s universal postal service is a government owed enterprise and has its own provision. Its provision, to some extent, has led the enterprise to become not only unprofitable but also suffer a deficit. To overcome this situation, China also initiated market-oriented services and is striving to actively compete, expand their market share and increase their postal income to meet social demands. In the 21st century, China’s postal service will be completely modernized. It will utilize the latest mechanization, automation and computerization, achieving rapid delivery, automated sorting, computerized operation, information-based management and other diversified services. The new system will play an important role in global postal affairs.

explanations.title: Learning objectives (Lesson 21, Seeing a Doctor, 看病)
explanations.body: Upon completion of this lesson you will be able to: ask for information about registering in a hospital; discuss your diseases and symptoms with a doctor and ask questions about examinations, taking medicines and filling prescriptions; describe your experience when seeing a doctor or going to an ER. To do so you must master the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section, the modal verb 应该/该 (能愿动词), the use of 那么/这么, the use of 别 (negative imperative), degree complements with 得 (程度补语), adjectives as predicates (2) (形容词谓语), adjectives used as adverbial adjuncts, the compound directional complement 起来 (趋向结构), the 把 construction with a locative complement and the use of 不要 (negative imperative). The Area Studies topic is China’s healthcare sector, promising for 2020 and beyond. The lesson belongs to Unit 4, Survival Skills and Social Factors.

examples.translation: guà hào shí tā děi mǎi yì běn bìng lì běn tián hǎo gè rén xìn xī rán hòu qù hòu zhěn shì lǐ děng zhe hù shì jiào hào jiào dào tā de hào shí tā jiù kě yǐ jìn qù kàn bìng le kàn guò yí cì bìng hòu xià cì zài qù kàn bìng kě yǐ zhí jiē yòng jiù zhěn kǎ zài wǎng shàng yù yuē fēi cháng fāng biàn dàn shì kàn bìng shí tā hái shì děi dài zhe bìng lì běn — When registering, she has to buy a medical record book and fill in her personal information, then wait in the waiting room for the nurse to call her number. When her number is called she can go in to see the doctor. After seeing the doctor once, next time she can use the patient card to make an appointment online directly, which is very convenient. But when seeing the doctor she still has to bring the record book. (Student B’s part; blanks mine)

examples.text: 琳达说，在中国看病跟在美国不一样。在美国看病，不需要去医院挂号，只要提前打电话或者上网预约就可以了。不过看病时也需要带着身份证和保险卡。
examples.translation: lín dá shuō zài zhōng guó kàn bìng gēn zài měi guó bù yí yàng zài měi guó kàn bìng bù xū yào qù yī yuàn guà hào zhǐ yào tí qián dǎ diàn huà huò zhě shàng wǎng yù yuē jiù kě yǐ le bú guò kàn bìng shí yě xū yào dài zhe shēn fèn zhèng hé bǎo xiǎn kǎ — Linda says that seeing a doctor in China is not the same as in the U.S. In the U.S. you don’t need to go to the hospital to register; you only need to call or book online ahead of time. But when seeing the doctor you also need to bring your ID and insurance card. (Student C’s part; blanks mine)

explanations.body: A. Study the diagram of the registration procedure at a Chinese hospital. B. Pair up.
